proposals.objective: Train a spatially weighted loss variant of the declined regime correction on the same split, offline and validation-only, weighting by local truth magnitude or by the metric's own point density, to test whether the error relocation was an artifact of equal-weight training
proposals.rationale: The regime model went NO-GO on its own pre-registered cap: the boundary moved instead of vanishing, which is the recorded mechanism finding, and the census showed the correction relocating error into the strip the metric weights least. That leaves one cheap, well-posed question: is the relocation a property of the correction or of the equal-weight loss it was trained under. A variant weighted by local truth magnitude or by the metric's own point density, trained on the same split with nothing else changed, answers it offline. Its pre-registration must state the same hurt-cap discipline that killed the predecessor, so a GO cannot be manufactured by weakening the rule that produced the NO-GO
proposals.gate: Pre-registered before training, carrying the same hurt-cap discipline that produced the predecessor's NO-GO. Outcome one: the weighted variant stops relocating error into the metric's weakly sampled strip on the validation split, so the relocation was an artifact of equal-weight training and a successor candidate has a stated mechanism. Outcome two: the relocation persists under weighting, so it is structural to the correction and the regime route stays closed on evidence. No test case is opened and no scoring call is made; the work is validation-only by construction
proposals.cost_basis: zero solver core-minutes, the review's own costing: offline fitting of the sklearn class on data already on disk, and the predecessor's measured cost was about two core-minutes of wall at a two-core cap, which is the scale expected here
proposals.expected_knowledge_gain: Whether the error relocation that ended the regime route belongs to the correction or to its training loss, which is the difference between a closed road and a mislabelled one, bought without opening a test case or launching a solver

proposals.objective: Adopt the rule that a model-form band states a containment verdict against a reference only at three or more converged members; below that the band reports its interval and says why no verdict is stated
proposals.rationale: The family-N a10 band demonstrated the failure this rule prevents, end to end and pre-registered: at n=2 the band missed the reference Cl by 0.22 percent and the negative-verdict review's entry 11 read the miss as under-membership rather than model-family failure; the pre-registered third-member arm then measured exactly that, with the SA member entering 0.051 below the two-member floor -- the n=2 band was a lower bound on the true spread by a factor of 2.4 on Cl -- and the reference moved from NOT contained to CONTAINED with no change to any member already present. A min-max interval over two draws from a model family is a lower bound on the family's spread, so a NOT-contained verdict at n=2 is a statement about membership, not about the family, and the batch's own design already refuses bands below two members for the same structural reason. The rule: containment verdicts (contained or not contained) print only for groups with three or more converged members; a two-member group prints its interval with the annotation that no containment verdict is stateable at n=2. Existing artifacts are regenerated, not rewritten by hand, and the flat-plate P_re2e7 group's containment lines are the known rows this rule will touch.
citations: The supervisor negative-verdict review of 2026-08-07, entry 11
The N a10 third-member pre-registration and its outcome section
The model-form band artifact, group N a10, n=2 and n=3 states
The model-form batch design, band rule section
proposals.cost_basis: measured at zero: the rule is a band-builder change plus a regeneration from records already on disk; no solver runs
proposals.expected_knowledge_gain: The band artifact stops being able to publish a membership artifact as a model-family verdict; the a10 case becomes the documented precedent with both states on the record

proposals.objective: Audit the F5c backward-facing step inlet against Driver and Seegmiller's stated boundary-layer development, verifying that our inlet reproduces the reference boundary-layer thickness at the step within the experiment's tolerance, before any new solve is spent on the case
proposals.rationale: The F5c record shows converged solves landing a factor of four to twelve short on reattachment and wandering across configurations, and the out-of-memory premise that once excused the case is dead, refuted by our own record. The classic backward-facing step trap is an inlet that never develops the boundary layer the experiment had at the step, and a miss this large smells like it. The reference states a developed layer of given thickness there. Reading our inlet and existing fields against that statement costs nothing, and the review orders it first for exactly that reason: it is the cheapest hypothesis and it must be cleared before the unsteady probe spends anything
proposals.gate: The audit reads our inlet condition and the existing solution fields and compares boundary-layer thickness at the step against the value and tolerance the experiment states. Outcome one: our thickness sits outside the tolerance, the inlet owns a share of the factor-of-four-to-twelve failure, and repairing inlet development precedes all further spending on the case. Outcome two: our thickness sits inside, the inlet is exonerated on the record, and the unsteady probe run becomes the next diagnostic in the declared order
proposals.cost_basis: zero compute: the audit reads the existing inlet specification and stored fields against the reference's stated thickness; no new solve is launched
proposals.expected_knowledge_gain: Either the mechanism behind the largest unexplained failure on the campaign record, found for free in the inlet, or a clean exoneration that licenses the unsteady probe as the next diagnostic, with the order of spending decided by evidence rather than appetite

proposals.objective: Bound what any attached-flow steady solution could deliver for the NREL Phase VI Sequence S torque at seven metres per second, by a zero-compute blade-element calculation from the published S809 polars and the verified chord and twist
proposals.rationale: The steady branch closed three ways: geometry exonerated to the millimetre, frame terms audited to source lines, initialisation tested single-variable, and the motoring limit cycle persisted through all of it. What no record yet holds is the hand calculation the case invites: blade-element torque at Sequence S from published S809 polars and the chord and twist this lab has already verified against the reference geometry. That number bounds every attached-flow steady solution at once. If it lands near the published plus 800 newton metre turbine-signed torque, the limit cycle is numerical or basin behaviour; if blade-element theory is itself ambiguous at tip speed ratio 5.4, the case is intrinsically unsteady and the transient branch stops being optional.
proposals.gate: The calculation is written down before any comparison: blade-element torque at Sequence S from published S809 polars and the verified chord and twist, with its sensitivity to polar source stated beside it. Outcome one: the blade-element torque lands near the published plus 800 newton metre turbine-signed value, so an attached steady solution exists in principle and the persisting limit cycle is numerical or basin behaviour. Outcome two: the blade-element result is itself ambiguous at tip speed ratio 5.4, so the case is intrinsically unsteady and the transient branch is mandatory. Either way the transient branch inherits a quantified bound
proposals.cost_basis: zero compute by construction: a blade-element hand calculation from published polars and the chord and twist already verified on the record; no solver is launched
proposals.expected_knowledge_gain: The cheapest decisive statement available about the F8 family: whether the steady branch failed because the flow refuses a steady description or because the solver sits in the wrong basin, which is exactly the fork the transient branch needs answered before it spends
citations: The supervisor review of standing negative verdicts, 2026-08-07, section 3
The F8 record gating the existing MRF blade forces against Hand and colleagues 2001, including the geometry exoneration
Hand, Simms, Fingersh, Jager, Cotrell, Schreck and Larwood, the NREL Unsteady Aerodynamics Experiment Phase VI report, 2001

proposals.rationale: Acts show per-channel numbers but no total. proposals.decision_note: Approved under Katie's standing authorization, 2026-07-31: 'You also have my OK for all ur proposals dont wait for me to confirm.' Blanket, not per-item, so the hardness floor and the cost basis still gate what actually runs.
proposals.outcome: The convention already existed and the rationale's own example was stale: the hump has printed a Total row since 31 July, 0.2200 in x/c over numerical 0.0002 and model form 0.220 with input stated unquantified. Root sum of squares over the quantified channels at 95 percent lives in one function, 11 acts route through it, and all 6 acts that quantify two or more channels already display a combined band, so the gate as written was met before this started. What was missing was the rule written down and anything checking it. Both now exist, and the check fails on 2 acts: the B-52 geometry study and the Ahmed body each put the settled-state scatter into the total while their own channel table reports input unquantified. On the filmed B-52 recording the two displayed channels combine to 0.006353 and the published band prints 0.0064, so the undisclosed term is at most 0.0011 and does not move the printed figure. It is a rule discrepancy, not a wrong number, and which way to close it is a decision for Katie: show the scatter as a channel, or move it to the numerical channel where settling noise belongs.

proposals.objective: Make mesh non-orthogonality a stated input to the numerical uncertainty, since it now predicts divergence
proposals.rationale: Five grids ordered by severe non-orthogonality reproduce a clean dose response: 0.59 percent solves two hundred iterations clean, 6.70 dies at 143, 19.30 at 16, 29.12 at 11. Aspect ratio and skewness do not order them at all, and the grid with the worst maximum of both is the one that solves. The lab reports non-orthogonality as a mesh quality gate and never carries it into the uncertainty a result quotes, so a mesh that nearly failed and one that passed comfortably produce numbers wearing identical bands.
proposals.cost_basis: estimate
proposals.gate: The numerical channel states the mesh non-orthogonality behind it, and a near-gate mesh is visibly distinguished from a clean one
proposals.expected_knowledge_gain: The lab now has a measured predictor of solver failure and does not use it anywhere a result is judged

proposals.objective: Replace the mesh-quality gate, which cannot distinguish a good mesh from one pressed against a ceiling
proposals.rationale: Across seventy mesh logs on this box, eight sit pinned at 64.6 to 65.0 and three at 74.3 to 75.0. Those clusters are not physics, they are two different maximum-non-orthogonality ceilings written into the recipes. The lab gate is set at seventy, between them, so any mesh pressing on its own constraint returns pass at sixty five or fail at seventy five and nothing in between. Two rungs of one body land six thousandths of a degree apart. A credential also blames its finest rung failing at 74.96 on refinement, and a replicate reaches 74.962 at a third the cells.
proposals.cost_basis: estimate
proposals.gate: The gate reads a quantity that is not pinned by the recipe, and every affected credential is regraded on it
proposals.expected_knowledge_gain: The gate has been returning a property of the mesh dictionary rather than of the mesh
proposals.outcome: DONE 2026-08-02 at ZERO solver compute. The gate now returns two values: the verdict, AND whether the verdict was decided by a measurement of the mesh or by a meshQualityDict ceiling (workflows.geometry_study.mesh_quality_reading, ceiling_pinned, mesh_pinning_notes; tests PinnedGateTests). MEASURED ACROSS ALL 98 log.checkMesh FILES ON THIS BOX: 9 meshes read 64.64-64.99 under the strict maxNonOrtho 65, 3 read 74.31-74.96 under the relaxed 75, and -- a second gate the item did not name -- 5 read 3.896-3.99994 under maxBoundarySkewness 4, with study-b52-finer2-uq at 3.9999437 clearing a 4.0 gate by 5.6e-05. MAX_SKEWNESS 4.0 IS the dictionary ceiling, so that gate cannot fail any mesh the dictionary held; MAX_NON_ORTHOGONALITY 70 sits between 65 and 75 and has no resolution on a pinned mesh. Tolerances (1.0 deg, 0.15) are read off the measured population: widest pinned gap 0.36 deg and 0.104, nearest unpinned reading 58.4 deg and 3.535. AN INDEPENDENT DEMONSTRATION, measured today for free by the resolution study: the SAME four background-division triples read 57.556/58.374/60.801/62.391 at refinement 3, spread over 4.83 deg, and 64.958/64.977/64.990/74.962 at refinement 4 -- three of them agreeing to 0.032 deg because they are reporting the same ceiling. HALF THE ITEM'S OWN PREMISE IS CORRECTED RATHER THAN SHIPPED: average non-orthogonality is unpinned but is NOT a discriminator -- the rae2822 O-grids, maxima 80.2-160.9 with no dictionary applied, average 9.05-11.13, the same 9.39-9.90 the accepted snappyHexMesh meshes read. It is reported and explicitly not gated on. The count of faces above threshold survives, with a caveat the rationale did not state: at checkMesh's own 70 deg threshold it PARTITIONS identically to the 70 deg max gate; what it adds is EXTENT, and its magnitudes are unpinned across two orders of magnitude. A PARSER DEFECT FOUND ON THE WAY: naca4412_credential_repair.parse_checkmesh matched only 'Max non-orthogonality = X', which OpenFOAM 2606 never prints, so every stored result.json under w3-naca4412-layered-replicates carries a cell count and a skewness and no angle at all, and the published replicate table's angles were read out of the logs by hand. EVERY AFFECTED CREDENTIAL REGRADED: ahmed_35 at 49.6 is unpinned and its pass is a measurement; the NACA 4412's graded fine rung now passes on 0 of 2,008,367 faces above 70 deg rather than on a 64.989619 that is 0.010 deg under the ceiling the recipe wrote, and the finer rung's failure is restated as 797 of 5,740,702 faces, 1.39e-04 -- real in kind, small in extent, and NOT the leading suspect for that ladder's non-monotonicity that its own record named. proposals.objective: State in the verification charter that dimensionality decides admission to the window and nothing else
proposals.rationale: Changing the assumed dimensionality divides every observed order by exactly 1.5 and leaves the extrapolated value and a conclusive ladder band untouched, because the refinement ratio raised to the order is invariant under the change. So the assumption cannot corrupt a band; it can only wrongly admit or wrongly reject one. That is a narrow and checkable consequence, and stating it stops the next reader treating the parameter as a general modelling choice.

proposals.objective: Add residual-stall, oscillatory-divergence, and Courant-excursion rules to the monitor, covering the calm failure modes the spike rule cannot see
proposals.rationale: The lab's own evidence documents a failure the current monitor misses by design: the Re 200 cylinder stalls at residual near 1e-3 with a small force oscillation and exits on the iteration cap looking calm, because a steady solver applied past its regime degrades measurably but never spikes. Detection rules from the monitor standard: a stall is a rolling-median residual improving by less than a factor of 2 over 200 iterations while still above the residualControl target; oscillatory divergence is alternating-sign residual changes with a growing envelope over 50 iterations; a Courant excursion is the reported maximum exceeding the case limit or growing monotonically over 20 steps. A stalled result is UNCONVERGED no matter how smooth its tail, and the prescribed action is the regime check before any rerun buys more iterations. The Courant rule is written now so the first transient run arrives born monitored.

proposals.objective: Back each fidelity chip with a compact credibility scorecard covering the two factors the chips do not encode: input pedigree and results robustness
proposals.rationale: Mapping the lab's four chips onto the NASA standard's assessment factors shows the chips already encode validation status, solver backing, and convergence. Two factors are invisible: input pedigree, so a run on poorly traced inputs can wear the same chip as one on measured inputs, and results robustness, so sensitivity knowledge never reaches the certificate. A per-result scorecard with a 0 to 4 level for each factor, following the standard's level definitions, closes the gap without changing what any chip means. The Womersley screening cap already behaves like the standard's placard requirement for use outside the validated domain, naming the limit, its extent, and the consequences; the scorecard states that explicitly. This is a content addition and may land directly on the certificate surfaces.
citations: NASA-STD-7009B, Standard For Models And Simulations, NASA 2024

THE 3x PLANNING MULTIPLIER BRACKETS 5 OF THE 15. Two land within 20 percent. The median ratio is 0.088, so the typical item cost a tenth of its estimate, while the worst over-ran at 13.55x -- a spread of 220 to 1 across the non-zero ratios, which is not a distribution a single factor describes. proposals.objective: Carry out Dow's statistical step on the field the CBFS inversion actually produced: fit the squared exponential covariance of the log discrepancy by maximum likelihood, and rule on whether that field is fit-able at all or is an artifact of an objective that cannot see it
proposals.rationale: The second of the three steps in Dow's structural-uncertainty method is a Gaussian random field fitted to the log discrepancy between the inferred and the modelled eddy viscosity, with a squared exponential covariance whose two parameters come from maximum likelihood. He reports the optimum for a straight channel and the correlation length he asserted for two-dimensional flows, and the whole step costs no solver time. This lab can run it today on machinery it already verified for a different purpose: the random matrix sampler carries a Nystrom solve of the covariance eigenproblem for an anisotropic squared exponential kernel, the truncated expansion, the interpolation from an auxiliary mesh to the mesh, and the field write path, and the whole chain was null tested by propagating an unperturbed field and recovering the baseline reattachment to one part in ten thousand. What is missing is a scalar variant of a tensor path and a two parameter likelihood maximisation, both arithmetic. The reason to run it now is not the fit but the diagnosis attached to it. The CBFS inversion plateaued at about 0.09 percent of its data term while its field moved substantially, reaching a multiplier of 0.735 in places, and the source method names exactly that combination: where the mean velocity gradient vanishes the objective is insensitive to the field, the sensitivity is identically zero there, and the field acquires structure the objective never sees, which does not spoil the velocity profile and does spoil any statistical model built on the field. Our objective carries a pull toward one and no smoothness term at all, so nothing in it addresses that null space. Fitting the covariance answers whether the moved cells sit where the adjoint has support or where it has none, and the same pass counts the cells where the stress limiter binds, which is where a multiplier on the omega equation cannot reach the eddy viscosity by the algebraic path. No solver runs and no flow case is started.

proposals.cost_basis: estimate, and the estimate is that no solver runs. The eigenproblem is dense and symmetric on a coarse auxiliary mesh; the earlier study used a fifty by thirty auxiliary mesh with thirty retained modes capturing 98.95 percent of the variance, and solved it in seconds. Every input field is already written to disk by runs that have been paid for
proposals.expected_knowledge_gain: Each outcome changes a decision. A covariance with a physically sensible correlation length, fitted on cells the adjoint can see, means the statistical step works here and the band program proceeds to propagation. A field whose structure sits in the objective's null space convicts the missing smoothness term rather than the method, and makes adding it a precondition on any future inversion run for an uncertainty purpose, at no solver cost per evaluation because its sensitivity is computed directly rather than through the adjoint. A field with no spatial structure at all says the inversion produced nothing to model and stops the band program before core-minutes are spent on sampling it. The limiter overlap count is a number nobody has, and it is the cheapest available test of the parameterization hypothesis behind the plateau

proposals.objective: Decide whether the NASA hump can be improved at all, given the benchmark ships no training data for it
proposals.rationale: After round 4 the NASA wall-mounted hump is the only case we are last on the board on, 0.0632 against a best of 0.0364, and our correction there is a regression against the uncorrected floor of 0.0621. The benchmark's own train/validation table has no hump entry -- it is test-only -- so the current prediction borrows the periodic-hill model on a pre-registered physical argument. Nobody has established whether a better legal choice exists or whether the honest answer is that the hump is unimprovable without outside data. That question is worth settling before more effort goes into the ducts, where we are already third of five.

proposals.decision: DECIDED 2026-08-01, decision half only, no solver and no scoring call. See demo-output/website/closure_challenge_C6_hump_decision.md. The premise is false and so is a sentence standing on the record. A legally trained route does exist: CBFS13700, the curved backward-facing step, is the benchmarks other single-variation case and it sits on the TRAINING side (README lines 71 to 77), it is the only two-dimensional smooth-wall separating and reattaching flow in the benchmark, and the pre-registered argument in train_closure_extended_correction.py lines 27 to 40 compares only periodic hills against ducts and never names it. The rules do not require a matching family: README line 65 says a submitter is free to use their own training and validation data and line 67 calls the split suggested; only the test cases are forbidden, line 63. So CLOSURE_CHALLENGE_STATUS.md lines 283 to 288, no action is available for NASA_2DWMH regardless, is withdrawn. Two actions are available. Route A, decline to correct the hump: the lab own train-side criterion already flags it out of the periodic-hill model training range on all 15 features at once from RANS-derived features with no ground truth read, and the tau normalisation audit shows why and shows it is algebraic, 20.0 percent of hump cells affected with I1 reaching 4.26e8 and a p90 of 23298.9, against 0 of 32 non-test cases carrying a single affected cell. Declining ships 0.0621 instead of 0.0632 and moves the entry from 0.0654314 to 0.0652939, which is 0.00014 and does not change the rank. Zero compute. Its weakness is stated: the criterion fires on a global covariate shift, not on the algebraically forced zero the decline gate was proven on. Route B, fit on CBFS: legal, closest flow in the benchmark, never tried, and it needs compute plus a pre-registration frozen before any scoring call. What genuinely constrains both is not the rules but the fact that the hump per-case score is already known from round 2, so whoever chooses now has seen it. Separately and not waiting: CLOSURE_CHALLENGE_SUBMISSION_DRAFT.md lines 69 to 73 quote the preprint permitting training on similar flows to the test cases, and that sentence is not in the benchmark clone, not in the eval package, not anywhere in this repository, and no copy of the preprint is on this box. The README carries the same permission in wording that is on disk.

proposals.outcome: Answered, and the gate's own binary turned out to be the wrong question. The gate asked for EITHER a legally-trained hump prediction beating 0.0621 on validation evidence alone OR a record that no such route exists. Neither is true: the route exists and is legal, and it cannot be demonstrated. Measured 2026-08-02, zero scoring calls, no model fitted, 51,626 hump cells read from the RANS field and mesh only with 0/U_LES, 0/k_LES and 0/tauij_LES never opened and named in the script so a reader can grep and confirm. Record: demo-output/website/closure_challenge_cbfs_donor_coverage.json, produced by sdk/scripts/closure_cbfs_donor_coverage.py. THE HUMP EXTRAPOLATES ON BOTH DONORS ON 7 OF 7 FEATURES, reproducing the earlier 'outside on all 15 features' finding through a different aggregation. CBFS covers better on 5 of 7 -- decisively on tke_ratio, 0.0004 of hump cells outside its range against 0.2697 outside the periodic hills' -- and WORSE on Re_y, 0.2615 against 0.1823, ceiling 30.25 against 38.08, p99 reaching 7.24 donor half-ranges past its edge against 5.55. Re_y is the one axis on which round 4 demonstrated with scores that extrapolation costs this entry points: 1.85x and 2.07x trained maximum on the two ducts it trails, 0.90x on the one it leads. The comparison is biased toward the periodic hills -- 327,600 cells across 21 cases against CBFS's 21,000 across one, 15.6x more data, and a convex hull can only widen with data -- and CBFS wins most of it anyway, which makes the Re_y loss harder to dismiss rather than easier. The Reynolds numbers are what topology hid: the benchmark states CBFS at Re_H=13700 in its own transportProperties and states none for the hump, recorded as absent rather than filled in, and the nearest READ source giving one is Buchanan, Lacatus, West and Dwight 2025 section 2.4 and Table 2, which trains on this same hump at Re_h = 9.3e5 against its own periodic hill at 1.0e4 and CBFS at 1.3e4. Both candidate donors sit within a factor of about 1.4 of each other and roughly seventy times below the target. WHAT WAS CORRECTED: the 2026-08-01 decision document argued Route B from flow topology alone and never checked it against the mechanism this lab had already proven, and that section now says so in its own voice. WHAT WAS DISMISSED: Route B is not taken, and the reason has changed from 'it costs compute' to 'no legal held-out flow in this benchmark is anywhere near the hump's Reynolds number, so nothing could show it beats 0.0621 before the single scoring call that would settle it'. proposals.objective: Extend the mesh gates with an advisory aspect-ratio rule and a volume-ratio warning, wired from the new mesh_quality section of the governed physics rules
proposals.rationale: The two hard gates the lab enforces, non-orthogonality 70 degrees and skewness 4, are exactly the acceptance thresholds compiled into checkMesh and stay unchanged. Two defensible gates are missing. Aspect ratio must enter as advisory only: the NASA TMR flat-plate reference grids on disk measure max aspect ratio 66643 to 74041 with zero non-orthogonality and machine-precision skewness, so a hard gate at the checkMesh reporting threshold of 1000 would reject every reference-grade boundary-layer grid; the defensible rule flags high aspect ratio only when it coincides with non-orthogonality above 60 degrees or skewness above 2. Volume ratio gets a warning below 0.01, the snappyHexMesh generation floor, catching abrupt cell-size jumps at refinement boundaries. Values and citations are already recorded in the governed physics rules under the mesh-quality section; this proposal is the enforcement wiring and the certificate note. The calibrated gate summary may also land directly as content on the mesh surfaces.

proposals.outcome: Six families fitted, and the bar the lab grades forecasts by turns out to be passable by a law that explains nothing. Every row is serial, evidenced from the runner rather than assumed, so core-minutes are wall seconds over 60 on this ledger and nowhere else. After dropping 1 torn line, 91 not-ok rows and the 6 stall rows above 3600 s, each family gets an a priori law on design parameters and an a posteriori law on its own size, trained on the first 80 percent in ledger order and graded on the last 20. Five of six clear three-consecutive-within-20-percent, and only three of those beat predicting the family's own median: vspaero-wing clears it 6,457 times in a row at R2 0.0002 while being 45 times worse than its median, and simplefoam-ahmed 17 of 17 while being 4.4 times worse. Every fit is now graded against that constant predictor. The laws that are real: unsteady cylinder wall time goes as Re^0.217, R2 0.972, holdout median error 1.9 percent, and as steps^1.156 with R2 0.992 and 0.67 percent; transonic NACA 0012 goes as mach^5.76, R2 0.818, 12.2 percent, and as iterations^1.026. Iterations carry an exponent of essentially 1 in both families that record them while within-family cell exponents are small, which is the arithmetic behind the flat plate overrun. The 69,223-row steady cylinder family stays at 47.6 percent median error and is a band rather than a point estimate. Found on the way: 56,190 of the 69,007 reduced-order rows, 27 percent of the whole ledger, record wall_seconds of exactly 0.0, so the 208,102 evaluation headline counts a quarter of itself at no measured cost. RESOLVED 2026-08-01 (escalation #2), and this study's reading of those zeros is withdrawn: it concluded they were two paths through the family, one recording nothing, inferred from the range of the positive values. Measured against the ledger instead, the positive values are piled on the rounding boundary rather than spread: 96.1 percent of the 12,817 non-zero reduced-order rows are at or below 0.003 s, median 0.001, and the smallest non-zero wall time anywhere in the ledger is exactly 0.001 s. There is one code path and one timer, mega_batch.py run_task lines 719 and 746, which stores round(seconds, 3), and the ROM replays at a median 0.000323 s, under the 0.0005 s boundary. The rows ran: 400 of 400 sampled zero-wall rows reproduce their recorded metrics exactly when the ROM is re-run on their own design. The zero share tracks host load in lockstep with the real solves sharing its index rota, 25.6 percent zeros on 07-23 at 8.85 s a cylinder row against 99.8 percent from 07-26 at 1.99 s. So the 208,102 count stands as measured; what does not stand is a measured cost for those rows, whose recorded 0.000 s is a floor. Core-hours were never unaffected by construction either, since lab_stats.ledger_summary sums these same wall_seconds, but the loss is bounded: under 0.0005 s per row, at most 28.1 s or 0.008 core-hours, 0.003 percent. The basis now sits in the credentials wall footer and in COST_SCALING.md section 6a.

proposals.objective: Make any tensor-basis closure report which of its ten coefficients its training data could constrain, before it is graded on a case of a different dimensionality
proposals.rationale: Read off Pope 1975 and checked to machine precision this session by the Pope 1975 basis check script: on any two-dimensional flow the fifth and tenth basis tensors are identically zero, so a ten-coefficient model trained only on two-dimensional families receives no gradient at all for two of its ten outputs, and the other eight enter only through three identifiable combinations. Seven of ten output degrees of freedom are unidentified. The tensors that vanish are the ones that carry a square duct's secondary flow, which is exactly the case the tensor-basis rung is meant to demonstrate. Separately, the basis is pointwise over-complete even in three dimensions: a symmetric traceless tensor has five independent components, the measured rank of the ten tensors is exactly five over two hundred random gradients, so a per-cell inversion for ten coefficients is ill posed and returns whatever the regulariser prefers. None of this is stated in either methods paper. A gate that computes the rank of the basis over a declared training set and names the unconstrained coefficients turns a silent extrapolation into a printed one.
citations: Pope, JFM 72 331 to 340, 1975, p. 334, READ IN FULL 2026-08-02
The W2 Pope 1975 integrity-basis record, section 2.2
The Pope 1975 basis check script in the lab's scripts tree

THE AUDIT, over 468 logs carrying both clocks under certonomous-runs and the solve registry: 67.77 CPU-hours inside 70.02 wall-hours, so 3.2 percent of all measured wall time in this lab was contention, time-weighted. proposals.objective: Measure the pointwise rank of the tensor basis on the actual duct baseline fields before the tensor-basis rung is scored a priori on them, and say how much of the anisotropy the representation can reach at all
proposals.rationale: Derived from Pope 1975 and checked to machine precision this session. A linear eddy viscosity RANS solve on a straight duct produces exactly zero secondary flow, which this lab already measured, so its mean field is unidirectional and its velocity gradient has one non-zero row. On such a field the ten basis tensors have pointwise rank exactly three, not five: singular values 5.474, 3.448, 2.235 and then 5.8e-16 and 3.1e-16, a clean gap. The fifth and tenth tensors are identically zero, so two of the ten coefficients have no effect. And a two-dimensional subspace of the symmetric traceless tensors cannot be produced by any values of the ten coefficients whatsoever, one of whose directions has zero streamwise row and column to 4.7e-16, a pure cross-plane tensor of the family this lab already names as b_yz and b_yy minus b_zz. The approved duct generalisation item specifies an a priori gate, beating the baseline on anisotropy RMSE against a held-out LES field, and that gate would be scored inside a representation that is rank three out of five at every cell. This is not an argument against the rung. Fed back into a solver the prediction generates secondary flow and the degeneracy disappears, so it is a property of the first iterate. It is an argument that the a priori number means something different from what it appears to mean, and that the difference is measurable in advance at no compute.

proposals.rationale: Zhao et al. 2020, read in full 2026-08-02, is the one closure paper of the three this lab has read that states the cost of its expensive step: the CFD-driven training typically requires order ten to the three CPU hours, and section 4.2 names the mechanism, that candidate models iterate through hundreds or thousands of generations and every generation runs its CFD calculations. Converted at this lab's own measured rates, one thousand CPU hours is sixty thousand core-minutes, which is ninety wall-hours or 3.8 days of the entire box at 11.06 cores sustained under MPI, 13.8 days at the 3.02 busy mean, and 29.8 days at the 1.40 long-run mean. A per-evaluation cross-check grounds it in this lab's own instrument rather than the paper's: the turbine meshes are about 62,086 cells, 10.2 percent larger than the 56,320-cell bump rung measured here tonight at 0.63 seconds per iteration serial at 56,320 cells per rank, so a 200-step candidate evaluation is about 2.1 core-minutes and the published search is roughly 28,000 evaluations. The whole approved W1 queue after this week's triage is 647 core-minutes, which is 1.1 percent of one such search. The method is genuinely attractive here for a reason the cost does not touch, and that is why the price needs writing down first: the cost function needs only a mean-flow profile at two stations rather than dense per-cell Reynolds stresses, so it is the one method of the three that this lab's sparse experimental data could feed. The failure mode this item prevents is proposing it on the strength of that attraction and discovering the price afterwards, which is the same shape of error that put a 603 core-minute item and a 240 core-minute item in the approved queue this week.
citations: Zhao, Akolekar, Weatheritt, Michelassi & Sandberg, RANS Turbulence Model Development using CFD-Driven Machine Learning, J. Comput. Phys. 2020, arXiv 1902.09075v2, sections 3.2 and 4.2, READ IN FULL 2026-08-02

proposals.outcome: READ IN FULL 2026-08-02 and indexed as claim, source, where-it-applies in demo-output/website/campaign/W2_POPE_1975_INTEGRITY_BASIS.md, with the basis stated in the lab's own notation and machine-checked: sdk/scripts/pope_1975_basis_check.py transcribes the ten tensors and five invariants off p. 334 and passes 13 of 13 checks, exit 0. All ten tensors symmetric and traceless to 3.5e-15 relative; the check has teeth, since writing 1/3 for the 2/3 in T6 leaves tr T6 = -3.98. Pope's own section 5 limit case is reproduced from the transcription to 4.4e-16 over 200 random (G0, G1, G2, k/eps, U_1,2), with no free parameter to absorb an error. Four findings that neither methods paper states. (1) The ten tensors are not Pope's: appendix A p. 339 says the three-dimensional procedure 'is reported by Spencer & Rivlin (1959, 1960) and the results for this situation are quoted in the text', so our citation was one level removed; both Spencer & Rivlin papers are closed on Unpaywall with 0 OA locations and are now on the library list. (2) Pope declares the three-dimensional form 'so intractable as to be of no value' and never determines its coefficients: the ten-tensor model does not exist in this paper, only the ten-tensor basis, so the tensor-basis network supplies by learning exactly what Pope declined to derive. (3) Pope's stated domain is a high-Reynolds-number NEARLY HOMOGENEOUS flow, with homogeneity of the rates of strain a necessary condition, which every case both approved rungs target violates. (4) The pointwise rank of the ten tensors is exactly 5 over 200 random three-dimensional gradients and exactly 3 in two dimensions, so ten coefficients are not identifiable per cell, and the exact two-dimensional reduction table derived here to 5.4e-16 shows T5 and T10 are identically zero: two of a ten-coefficient model's outputs receive no gradient from any amount of two-dimensional training data, and the other eight enter only through three combinations. Also caught: Pope's a = <uu>/k - (2/3)I is exactly twice Ling's b = <uu>/(2k) - (1/3)I, so a coefficient fitted against b is half Pope's G for the same flow. Also confirmed at zero compute: the premise of closure-duct-tensor-basis-carrier is an exact identity of any unidirectional field, not a property of its eight duct solves, with lambda2 = -lambda1, lambda3 = lambda4 = 0 and lambda5 = -lambda1^2/2 to 0.0e+00 residual. Charter section 6 triggers 2 and 4 fired; two proposals filed, w2-identifiable-tensor-coefficients-gate and w2-tensor-basis-convention-declaration. Cost: 0 core-minutes against a 0 core-minute estimate, no solver launched. Extended the same session onto the duct, the tensor-basis rung's own demonstration case, at zero compute. A linear-eddy-viscosity duct baseline is unidirectional -- this lab measured that -- so its velocity gradient has one non-zero row and the ten tensors have pointwise rank exactly 3 over 500 random two-component gradients, singular values 5.474, 3.448, 2.235, 5.8e-16, 3.1e-16. T5 and T10 are identically zero there too, so the two coefficients 2-D training cannot constrain are also the two the duct cannot exercise, and a 2-dimensional subspace of anisotropy is unreachable by ANY values of the ten coefficients, one of whose directions is a pure cross-plane tensor with zero streamwise row and column to 4.7e-16. This corrects the lab record twice. W2_TBNN_SPARTA_READING.md says of the duct that 'all ten of Pope's tensors are live': true of the output anisotropy, not of the input basis built from a unidirectional baseline. And closure_challenge_duct_anisotropy_expressivity.json concludes 'Effective feature count for this flow family is 5, not 7' -- it is 3, because that audit named the two invariants that VANISH but not the two that are DETERMINED, lambda2 = -lambda1 and lambda5 = -lambda1^2/2, both visible in its own published correlation table where every Pearson r against I2_W2 is the exact negative of the one against I1_S2. The vanishing of lambda3 and lambda4 was already proved by that audit and is credited, not re-claimed. Third proposal filed: w2-duct-baseline-basis-rank-before-the-tbnn-rung. The check script is now 16 of 16, exit 0.

proposals.objective: Require every tensor-basis implementation to declare its anisotropy and strain-rate conventions and to reproduce Pope's own worked limit case before its coefficients are compared to anything
proposals.rationale: Both papers are now READ IN FULL and the ten tensors are identical between them, term for term, so the transcription is checked against two independent printings. The object they multiply is not identical. Pope normalises the anisotropy as the Reynolds stress over k less two thirds of the identity; Ling's own text prints it over twice k less one third. They differ by exactly a factor of two, verified to zero residual, so a coefficient fitted against one is half the other for the same flow and must never be compared to the coefficients Pope prints in his equation 4.3 without it. Worse, and this is the part that cannot be patched afterwards, the strain-rate convention is not printed at all. Ling states only that S and R were non-dimensionalized using the turbulent kinetic energy k and the turbulent dissipation rate as suggested by Pope; there is no equation defining either tensor anywhere in the manuscript and no explicit factor, so Pope's one half in his equations 3.2 and 3.3 has to be assumed rather than read. That assumption is not small, because Pope's tensors are of mixed degree in the strain and rotation rates. Dropping the one half scales the ten tensors by 2, 4, 4, 4, 8, 8, 16, 16, 16 and 32 respectively and the five invariants, which are the model's own input features, by 4, 4, 8, 8 and 16. A convention error is therefore not one constant a fitted coefficient absorbs: it is a different factor on each of the ten coefficients and a simultaneous rescaling of every input the model reads, and a model trained under one convention and evaluated under the other is wrong in a way no single number repairs. This is catchable at zero compute, because Pope's section 5 prints five component expressions for a simple shear flow that any correct implementation reproduces with no free parameter to hide an error in, and this lab's transcription already does so to four parts in ten thousand million million.
citations: Pope, JFM 72 331 to 340, 1975, equations 3.1 to 3.3 and section 5 p. 336, READ IN FULL 2026-08-02
Ling, Kurzawski & Templeton, SAND2016-7345J, manuscript p. 6, equations 1 and 2, READ IN FULL
The W2 Pope 1975 integrity-basis record, sections 2.3 and 2.4
The Pope 1975 basis check script in the lab's scripts tree
proposals.cost_basis: estimate; a declaration and a unit test, no solver
proposals.expected_knowledge_gain: A factor of two between a published coefficient and ours is indistinguishable from a modelling result until somebody writes the convention down

proposals.objective: Close the four structurally echo-less lever classes found by the dead-lever audit: every load-bearing solver lever must either print its own runtime banner (sub-LU style) or be echoed into the run log by the launcher at t=0, so charter v1.5 section 9 levers_verified_active is satisfiable at write time instead of failing retroactively

The positive template already exists in the lab twice over: the DALinearEqn sub-LU patch prints 'DAFOAM_SUBPC_TYPE=lu: ASM sub-block PC set to complete LU' at activation, the archive holds a negative control proving the off-state (cbfs_regress log: no banner, reason -9), and every conclusion-bearing sub-LU run asserts the banner before trusting the result; DAFoam's daOptions dump and OpenFOAM's turbulence-model printCoeffs are the same pattern natively. Proposed mechanics, report-only, for Infra to adopt with their own verification: (a) the common launch wrappers (the sanctioned solve launcher and the sdk workflow builders that assemble cases) echo the scheme dictionary, the solution dictionary, the MRF and thermophysical dictionaries and the boundary-condition files into the run log before invoking the solver, delimited with a LEVER-ECHO header and the case path plus a sha256 of each file so the echo is bound to the artifact that ran; (b) any lab-built patch that adds a lever must print an activation banner AND leave a distinguishable off-state (the sub-LU B-1 hazard -- unrecognized env values silently fall back to stock with no tell -- is what the banner-assert discipline exists to catch; new patches should hard-fail on unrecognized values instead of falling through); (c) the record-writing convention gains the assertion pattern: a levers_verified_active entry cites either the code's own banner line or the launcher's LEVER-ECHO block line, and a pre-registration naming a lever from classes 1-4 is rejected at filing unless the plan's launcher does the echo. proposals.rationale: Found 2026-08-02 while fixing the bump ladder's own collector, and reported rather than edited because the mega-batch workflow is a shared module whose tests were red from another well's in-flight work at the time. OpenFOAM renames a function object's output by appending the restart time when the file already exists on a restart. The lab already knows this for the coefficient history, and the bump ladder's stitcher handles it for the force histories; the TMR verification workflow reads both the coefficient files and the wall-shear files through wildcards and so is safe. The one function object nobody wildcarded is y+. In the bump ladder this published the medium rung's y+ from iteration 5,000 beside a Cd from iteration 16,000, recovered only by reading the renamed, time-suffixed y+ file that sat beside a header-only original; the correction moved the numbers by 0.002 to 0.02 percent, small in magnitude and not in kind. The mega-batch collector sorts a recursive glob for the bare y+ filename and feeds the last match straight into its y+ gate, which raises when it fails, so this is a GATE reading a possibly stale value rather than a reported number. Two things make it latent rather than armed, and both need checking rather than assuming: a single-run case never triggers the rename, and the sort is over path strings so directories sort lexically while they are named for a run's start time in any case. The question is whether any mega-batch row has ever been restarted, and the ledger can answer it.
citations: Bump ladder campaign record, NASA grids, section 6
Bump ladder collection script, the repaired collector
Mega-batch workflow, the y+ gate read
TMR verification workflow, the wildcarded reads that are the counter-example
proposals.cost_basis: estimate; a read over the existing ledger plus at most a few lines of collection code and its test. No solver. The equivalent fix in the bump collector took no compute at all
proposals.expected_knowledge_gain: A gate that raises on a value it may have read from the wrong iteration is worse than a reported number that is wrong, because it decides rather than informs

The retrospective found zero affected rows: all 52 Ahmed ledger rows are single-attempt, every attempt builds in a wiped case directory since the family's first commit, and the 17 surviving case directories hold no renamed file, no multi-run time directory and no header-only original. proposals.outcome: Taken by withdrawal, not by a gate. Supervisor ruling R1 answers conflict C-2 with option B, against the lab's own recommendation of C, on the grounds that C buys a measurement of the gate and the gate was never the problem. Five measurements are kept beside the entry in docs/standards/MONITOR_STANDARD.md rather than deleted with the rule. (1) Fire rate over all 106 archived steady solver logs, ungated: fires on 68, reaches FATAL on 65, and every one of those runs completed with its results on the record, so it was calling about two thirds of the lab's healthy steady work divergent. (2) Four tightenings, none of which rescued it: requiring the residual level to stop improving still gives 68 logs; requiring a full window of persistence gives 40; measuring growth against a 200 iteration baseline gives 59; raising the growth factor to four times gives 23. (3) The one that decided it, on the case the rule was written for: 22 firings on the sick log against 20 on the healthy one, the same number to within the rule's own noise, so it does not separate them. (4) Why no threshold saves it: the ratio of one noise envelope to the next on a converged flat field is close to a coin toss, so the fire rate is a function of run length rather than run health. (5) Four archived transient runs, taken 2026-07-30, fired 5, 5, 6 and 9 times, all completed healthily, all false positives; that measurement was the reason for the steady-solve scoping and is now the reason for nothing. The shipped gate was never a measurement: the archive does not record the residual target each run aimed for, so the corpus cannot be replayed with the gate in place and its false-positive rate is unmeasured and unmeasurable with the data the lab holds. Withdrawn from the standard, which goes to version 1.2 and becomes the first version to remove a rule rather than add one, leaving section 3.2's category empty and its failure family named as uncovered; and withdrawn from the code, with no disabled or dead-code detector left behind because one left in the module gets rewired. sdk/tests/test_log_signatures.py asserts detect_oscillatory_divergence stays absent and sdk/tests/test_head_engineer.py asserts the 'oscillatory-divergence' anomaly kind stays absent, so re-adding either fails the suite rather than passing quietly. S10, which names exactly one log out of 383, stands, and so does S10a. Spent 0 core-minutes against a 0 core-minute estimate: every number above is a replay of files already on disk. NOT A GENERAL VERDICT ON THE OTHER RULES, and the replay that came with it says so: S4 fires on 158 of 449 logs and 38923 findings while the WATCH-then-FLAG severity ladder section 1 describes for it exists nowhere in the code, and S5's entire vocabulary over the archive is 2 distinct keys, both artefacts of the key rather than facts about the logs, because OpenFOAM puts its warning text on the lines after the banner so 146 logs collapse onto one contentless key and the normaliser's number class swallows e, E, dot and hyphen so allowSystemOperations keys as allowSyst#mOp#rations. Both are recorded in section 3.5 beside their rules. Neither detection is changed here: standing rule 4 sends a detection change through the innovation path with the measurement attached.

proposals.outcome: Swept, and the premise holds but is narrower than filed in one direction and worse in another. All 27 checks in scripts/self_audit.py were read and each now declares, in a BASIS table the audit itself enforces, which of five things it tests, what it catches and what it is blind to. The tally over the 29 checks that now exist: 9 EVIDENCE (re-derive a published number from a primary artifact by arithmetic the audit performs itself), 11 PROPERTY, 4 SURFACE, 2 GENERATOR, 1 TRANSCRIBED, 2 META. THREE OF 29 CANNOT FAIL ON A DEFECT IN THE CODE OR CONSTANTS THEY CHECK. (1) check_wall_credentials_vs_results, the one this item was filed on: it calls chief_engineer.lab.displayed_credential at self_audit.py:696 and sdk/scripts/build_wall.py calls the same function at line 83 to write the card, so the Ahmed 25 degree area-basis defect was on both sides and it read PASS before the fix and PASS after. One arm of it IS independent: relative_error is recomputed there from the result file's own cd_compared and reference_cd. (2) check_gate_table_vs_transcripts imports scripts/gate_table.py and compares its fresh output to the published NINE_ACT_GATE_TABLE.md, which is that same generator's output pasted into markdown; it catches drift and a transcript that stopped supporting a row, and a misparse inside gate_table.py agrees with itself. (3) The worst is check_cost_predictions, which the filing did not name: its entire evidence is three tuples typed into the audit file, so it reads nothing on disk and cannot fail on a wrong pair at all, while 26 of the 57 completed docket items state a measured core-minute figure in their outcome and none is in that list. Nine checks are genuinely independent and the shape to copy is check_f2_reproduction, which parses postProcessing/forceCoeffs1/0/coefficient.dat itself. Three more carry couplings that are real but not of this kind and are now stated: check_memory_scaling_law refits the law correctly and reads its three measurements out of the same document that states the law, so a mistyped MiB figure refits to the mistyped law; check_fd_grades_current_standard reads the percentage off the published row and never recomputes it, and its _fd_grade restates verification charter section 7 as literals; check_declined_ladders_name_their_guard compares two fields the same writer wrote from the same fit and never refits to confirm either. FOUND ON THE WAY, and left as an open finding: THE AUDIT DOES NOT AUDIT ITSELF. _py_sources() covers sdk/workflows and sdk/chief_engineer only, so scripts/ is outside the reach of check_restated_thresholds, and self_audit.py's own two restated constants, _fd_grade's 15.0/5.0 and STALL_SECONDS, are invisible to the check that exists to find exactly that. proposals.outcome: Swept, and the two writers the item was filed on were already repaired, so what this closes is the general half of the gate: the audit now checks it. Both study writers route through uq.study_numerical, which copies the fit wholesale and names its three exclusions in STUDY_NUMERICAL_DROPS with a reason per key, and writes `dropped_from_fit` onto the record. lab.credential_card does the same through CREDENTIAL_NOT_ON_CARD. Those two are the accepted remedies and the check names both with their in-tree precedent. THE SWEEP, over sdk/workflows, sdk/chief_engineer and sdk/scripts: 22 sites build a dict from one source with four or more hand-typed keys. ONE clears (lab.credential_card, which also copies shown.items()). TWO take that source as a PARAMETER, so the function cannot see what its caller put in it and the author cannot know the key set: sdk/chief_engineer/lab.py:629 displayed_credential(), which builds the display block from `record` with 6 hand-typed keys, and sdk/workflows/geometry_study.py:774 mesh_validity(), which builds from `wall` with 4. NINETEEN more have the same shape on a source built a few lines up, where the author can see the keys; those are the weaker case and ride on the report as a census. displayed_credential is the one that matters, and the reason is the same path this week's other defect lived on: it is the function every credential card is built through, it takes the stored result file as a parameter, and a field added to a result file is dropped from every card in silence. Its own module already carries the remedy twenty lines below it. Fixing it changes what the wall shows, so it is left as a named finding with a remedy rather than edited here, and belongs with whoever holds the wall. WHAT THE CHECK HONESTLY MEASURES, stated in its BASIS entry rather than implied: the shape is the precondition for the defect and not the defect. A whitelist whose source has exactly the keys it copies is correct and nothing static distinguishes the two -- mesh_validity is very likely that case. So the verdict is WARN, the parameter-sourced case is separated from the local one, and the check is declared PROPERTY rather than EVIDENCE. Zero compute against a zero estimate.

proposals.objective: Give the mesh birth-certificate rule (Verification Charter v1.5 section 9) its mechanics: the certificate lives beside the mesh, hash-bound to it, and every workflow that lets a mesh enter a case asserts it at entry
proposals.rationale: The 2026-08-08 archive sweep (the mesh birth-certificate audit record of 2026-08-08) found 178 unique reachable meshes: 105 already certified, 47 clean-but-uncertified, and exactly one born broken -- the A3 vcoarse pyHyp mesh, which entered a case three times under reconstruction because nothing at entry asked for its certificate. The single biggest gap is structural, not individual: the mesh cache stores bare polyMesh with no quality record, so 400+ act-six, act-seven, act-nine and study run dirs carry a mesh with no record beside it even though geometry_study's gate DID run checkMesh at generation -- the reading was transient (L-40: the switch that ran must be provable from the artifact). Proposed mechanics, report-only, for Infra to adopt with their own verification: (1) certificate = log.checkMesh beside the case (existing convention) plus a hash-bound certificate sidecar beside every .mesh-cache entry carrying points_sha256, verdict, cells, maxAR, maxNonOrtho, maxSkew, generator, created_at. (2) Insertion points: the head engineer's mesh-cache save (~line 1006) writes the certificate at cache-save; cached_mesh_available (~971) treats a cache entry without a matching-hash certificate as NOT cached, which is the charter's quarantine; restore_cached_mesh (~986) asserts hash+verdict at entry and copies the certificate into the case. the DAFoam docker engine's mesh-cache mirror (~lines 216 to 250) gets identical mechanics -- this is the pyHyp entry path, the pathology's generator. the geometry workflow persists the log its gate judged (mesh_quality_reading ~455, retry_mesh_quality ~590, rung builder ~1388-1402) into the case dir and hands it to save_mesh_to_cache. the model-form batch script, already the exemplar (retained logs, hard gates at mesh_verdict ~569), adds assert-at-entry so an absent or unreadable log.checkMesh refuses the solver launch instead of surfacing as post-hoc exclusion. (3) Pre-registrations and docket items naming a mesh rung carry its points_sha256 plus verdict so a born-broken mesh cannot re-enter under a new case name.
citations: The mesh birth-certificate audit record of 2026-08-08
The verification charter, section 9, mesh birth certificate
The lessons record, L-40 companion paragraph
The A3 sub-LU result record, where the born-broken specimen is indicted
proposals.cost_basis: measured; the audit's own 85 s of serial checkMesh is already spent, the mechanics themselves are code changes with no solver time
proposals.expected_knowledge_gain: Every mesh that enters an archive, a pre-registration, or a ladder rung is provably born clean at the artifact level, and a missing certificate is a refusal at entry rather than a forensic finding months later; the A3 vcoarse failure mode (same broken mesh, three case reconstructions, zero certificate checks) becomes unreachable
proposals.outcome: Adopted as Mesh Standard v1.1 section 6 after the supervisor re-verified the audit by hand: the born-broken A3 vcoarse specimen's checkMesh reproduces digit-for-digit (aspect ratio 2.08e95, 23 negative-volume cells), a born-clean certificate reproduces digit-for-digit, and the dedupe-by-points-hash claim holds. Implemented at all three mesh-cache layers plus a fourth chokepoint the proposal missed (the shock-bench module cache two unsteady workflows share): certificate at save from the case's own checkMesh record, quarantine at lookup for any entry without a matching-hash accepted certificate, certificate carried into the case at restore, the geometry workflow saving after its gate so the certificate is the gate's own persisted reading, and the model-form batch refusing a launch on an uncertified or breaching mesh with R12 exemptions preserved. proposals.objective: Read the twelve dismissed proposals together and name what made them dismissible
proposals.rationale: Dismissals went from two to twelve in a day, and every one was caught by the agent that took the item rather than at drafting. That is the process working, and it is also twelve pieces of evidence about how these get written badly. Several are already known: a premise stated as fact when it was an inference, a record searched in one directory and declared absent, a convention called missing when six acts already had it. Read as a set they should say which drafting habits produce them.
proposals.cost_basis: estimate
proposals.gate: The dismissed set is characterised, and at least one drafting rule is added that would have caught several
proposals.expected_knowledge_gain: A queue whose items are wrong on arrival spends the attention of whoever picks each one up
proposals.decision_note: Approved under Katie's standing authorization, 2026-07-31: 'You also have my OK for all ur proposals dont wait for me to confirm.' Zero compute; the box was oversubscribed and this item was scoped to spend none.
proposals.outcome:
Read as a set they are not twelve mistakes, they are one drafting habit and two templates. TEN OF THE TWELVE WERE GENERATED RATHER THAN WRITTEN. Four came from a stored ladder verdict and share their last sentence verbatim, 'A further rung can settle the observed order': agp-beadb3545c04 on the B-52, agp-f493fff26990 on the NACA 4412, agp-11fa38e9a055 on the Ahmed 35, agp-130bfe3b2961 on the motorbike. Six came from a mission report's own next-steps prose and all open 'Filed under next investigations by the mission report'. The remaining two were hand written: w2-pope-1975-before-the-methods-that-use-it duplicated an item that closed the same day, and agp-4369c99cdd7f asked for nine rungs of an experiment already priced at 11,700 core-minutes for one.

THE COMMON DEFECT IS ONE SENTENCE. Each restated a CONCLUSION from a record and then supplied its own DIAGNOSIS, without opening the record. 'The refinement study ended inconclusive' is a symptom; 'a further rung can settle the observed order' is a cause the item invented. The true cause was elsewhere every time. On the B-52 the fifth rung already existed, and so did the sixth and the seventh. On the 4412 the quoted sequence belonged to a ladder retired on 2026-07-27 for having no boundary-layer cells. On the Ahmed 35 the three rungs are two mesh recipes, so the fitted order crosses a step that is not a refinement. On the motorbike the finest increment already sat below its own iterative noise floor, so a finer rung shrinks it further. A stored VERDICT is not the record; the file holding the rungs is the record.

NOT ONE OF THE TWELVE FELL ON COST. Eight were priced at exactly 20 core-minutes and two at exactly 60, the drafter's default, 883 core-minutes in total, and the price was never the reason any of them failed. Ten of the twelve were filed on 2026-07-25 and sat in the queue until 2026-07-31 or later, presenting as runnable to every agent that scanned the docket, until the first one who opened the artifact killed them. Every reason is on the record, in dismiss_reason for ten of them and in outcome for the other two, which is itself worth knowing: a reader asking why something was dismissed has to check two fields.

THE RULES ADDED, both with the archive replay charter 4 disqualifier 10 demands. Disqualifier 11, a premise quoted from a stored artifact that nobody opened: 13 proposals quote a numeric sequence in their rationale and NOT ONE of the 13 carries a citation that resolves to a file in this tree; 4 are dismissals and 6 more reached done only after the agent who took them corrected the premise in the outcome. Disqualifier 12, a rationale transcribed from another document's next steps: 9 proposals, 6 dismissed and 3 approved at zero core-minutes, repriced to unknown and blocked on a meshed valve and a moving-boundary solver this box does not have. Nine of nine never became runnable work. agenda.premise_violations implements both, fires on 22 of 209, and catches 10 of the 12. It is ADVISORY rather than a refusal for a reason unrelated to its hit rate: rule 11 asks a proposal to cite the file holding the numbers it quotes, and the style rail forbids a file reference in a citation, which 202 citations on this docket already break. That conflict predates this item and is escalated, not resolved. Replayed in the test suite rather than only when remembered.

THIS ITEM'S OWN PREMISE IS CORRECTED. It names three examples, a premise stated as fact when it was an inference, a record searched in one directory and declared absent, and a convention called missing when six acts already displayed it. None of the three is among the twelve dismissals. All three belong to w8-a-premise-can-be-false-and-still-worth-filing, which is about items closed as CORRECTED rather than dismissed. The two sets were merged in the drafting, and the merge turns out to be the finding: the same defect produces both outcomes, which is exactly what the replay measures at 4 dismissed and 6 corrected out of the 13 that fire. Cost: 0 core-minutes of solver time against a 0 core-minute estimate.

proposals.objective: Require an uncertainty budget to name its largest term and stop work on the others
proposals.rationale: Multifidelity fusion cut the race estimator error by a factor of 33, and the budget it produced showed that the estimator was then no longer the largest contributor: the solver model-form term, never measured, was. Further tightening of the estimator would have been effort spent on the term that had already stopped mattering. A budget that does not rank its own terms invites exactly that.
proposals.cost_basis: estimate

proposals.expected_knowledge_gain: Stops the lab optimising the term it can already measure instead of the one that dominates
proposals.decision_note: Approved under Katie's standing authorization, 2026-07-31: 'You also have my OK for all ur proposals dont wait for me to confirm.' Blanket, not per-item, so the hardness floor and the cost basis still gate what actually runs.
proposals.outcome: The charter half landed last night (b3524525, RESULT_PRIORITY_CHARTER section 4.5) and the enforcement half did not, so a budget could still be written that ranks nothing. It cannot now. uq.combine_expanded, the one function every budget in this lab routes through and which 13 acts and the race budget script call, returns largest beside contributions and missing: the largest term it was given, its value, and its share, named share_of_quantified_total and carrying ranks_only_what_was_measured, because a share of a total taken over the quantified channels alone is not a share of the uncertainty. A missing term is not a small term, and largest is reported next to missing rather than instead of it. The race budget was re-derived in place from its own stored contributions, which reproduces combined_95 at 0.2193838645571713 to the last digit and the missing list unchanged, so no measurement was repeated and no number moved: the largest quantified term is the input spread at 0.21937707698304945, 99.997 percent of the combined figure; the estimator is 0.0017257237358500922, 0.79 percent, and it is the SMALLEST term in the budget after fusion cut it by a factor of 33 from 0.02832 to 0.00086; the high-fidelity model form is still null. Tests: sdk/tests/test_uq.py 49 passed and 23 subtests, sdk/tests/test_race_study.py 46 passed. verify_warm_replay: nasa-hump IDENTICAL 29s, geometry-study IDENTICAL 31s, ahmed-body IDENTICAL 26s.

proposals.objective: Rule on nine approved follow-ons that may sit below the hardness floor
proposals.rationale: Nine of the twelve approved items are agenda-generated follow-ons on the vortex-lattice airliner and the analytic valve: composite span limits, a cruise Mach trade, drag under yaw, the next body in the class, a full-configuration solve. The case-selection charter puts a floor at HARD, meaning three-dimensional separated flow, shocks, unsteady statistics, free surface, rotating or challenge-aligned, and requires anything below it to be labelled a regression test. Several of these are screening studies on a panel method. Worse, the model-form error of that panel method against truth is unquantified and is now the largest term in its own error budget, so more studies on it refine the term that has already stopped mattering.
proposals.cost_basis: estimate
proposals.gate: Each of the nine is either shown to clear the floor, relabelled a regression test, or dismissed
proposals.expected_knowledge_gain: Twelve approved items and 1400 core-minutes of queue should not rest on a floor nobody checked them against
proposals.decision_note: Approved under Katie's standing authorization, 2026-07-31: 'You also have my OK for all ur proposals dont wait for me to confirm.' Blanket, not per-item, so the hardness floor and the cost basis still gate what actually runs.
proposals.outcome: Ruled 2026-08-02 at 0 core-minutes against a 0 core-minute estimate, no solver launched; full ruling in demo-output/website/campaign/W1_HARDNESS_FLOOR_RULING.md. Of the nine, THREE clear the floor and SIX are dismissed, and none is relabelled a regression test. The three that clear -- agp-527efc1cbb44 harmonic-balance, agp-a3cc843ce473 resolve-the-shedding, agp-37da30f972b3 unsteady FSI -- all clear on criterion 3, unsteady statistics, and every one of the three had the same defect the six had: a 60 core-minute estimate that is the drafter's default rather than an estimate. Two of the three are blocked on capabilities this box does not have (no meshed valve, no moving-boundary transient solver) and the third is blocked on a re-scope, because the parent solve's freestream is uniform (15 -0 -0) with no cross-flow component and there is no shedding at that condition to resolve. All three re-priced to unknown. None of the six can be relabelled a regression test, and that is the finding: the charter defines a regression test as a run whose expected value is written down beforehand, and every one of the six sweeps a NEW design point -- a span beyond today's cap, a cruise Mach not yet flown, a yaw angle not yet run, a body not yet chosen -- so there is no prior number to regress against. They are neither HARD nor regression tests; they are new easy results, which is the category the floor exists to prevent. Three of the item's own premises were corrected. The queue is 19 approved W1 items and 1,843 core-minutes, not twelve and ~1,400; it grew by seven items and 443 core-minutes in the two days the ruling sat unmade. The nine come from THREE parent studies, not two: the airliner (VSPAERO vortex-lattice), the valve (an algebraic orifice correlation that solves nothing), and the NACA 4412 finite wing (steady RANS in simpleFoam, not a panel method), three follow-ons each. And the airliner's model-form error is not the largest term in its budget, it is the term with NO number in it: mfmc_error_budget.json carries high_fidelity_model_form null and combined.missing [model], with the largest QUANTIFIED term the input spread at 0.21938, 99.997 percent of the quantified total, and the record already self-flags ranks_only_what_was_measured true. The item's conclusion survives all three corrections and two of them sharpen it. Net: approved W1 drops from 19 items to 12 and from 1,843 declared core-minutes to 1,463. That 380 comes off in two ways and the second is the larger: 200 core-minutes withdrawn by the six dismissals, and 180 withdrawn by RE-PRICING the three items that clear the floor, each of which carried the same default 60 and is now est_core_min 0 with cost_basis unknown -- not because they are cheaper but because nobody had estimated them at all. That is the return: 'approved, 60 core-min' read identically on the three items that clear the floor and the six that do not, and no reader of the queue could have told them apart.

proposals.outcome: Ruled, and the ruling had already gone the item's way on the tier: the Ahmed 25 deg row is SOLVER-BACKED at 0.3041 with the reason naming its inconclusive ladder, and there is no VALIDATED row left on the wall (commit e2e2d983). Verified 2026-08-01 that the wall and its generator agree exactly: build_wall._credentials_from_disk re-derived all 8 cards and every field matched the published wall.json, and self_audit's wall check reports PASS. The gate's second half did not hold. The card publishes measured on the reference's frontal-area basis (0.3041 from the production rung's 0.08481, ratio 3.586) but took its envelope straight off the study's band_abs, which fits on the rungs' planform basis, so it printed +/-0.02 beside 0.3041. A reader divides those and gets 6.65% where the study's own band_rel is 23.85%. displayed_credential now rebases the band on the same ratio as the value: the row reads +/-0.073 and the two bases agree. The other two banded rows sit at ratio 1.0 and did not move (cube +/-0.0078 against band_rel 0.709%, NACA 0012 wing +/-0.015 against 125.45%). Why no check caught it: self_audit compares the wall against a re-derivation through the same function, so an error inside that function is identical on both sides and reads as agreement; test_uq's rebasing test asserted the rebased value and not the envelope, and now asserts both. proposals.objective: Stop the proposal style rails reading a quoted numeric ratio as a file path and dropping the proposal

proposals.objective: Teach the weekly audit to catch the shipped bundle falling behind the tree
proposals.rationale: The laptop bundle was 32 commits behind: 21 modules and the control room drifted, and one module was absent entirely. It shipped a certificate that captioned any envelope a 95 percent confidence interval. Nothing detected any of it. The one bug that was found was found by hand, on a different errand.

proposals.expected_knowledge_gain: The artifact people actually run stops silently diverging from the one that is tested
proposals.decision_note: Approved under Katie's standing authorization, 2026-07-31: 'You also have my OK for all ur proposals dont wait for me to confirm.' Blanket, not per-item, so the hardness floor and the cost basis still gate what actually runs.
proposals.outcome: check_bundle_drift is in scripts/self_audit.py and in the CHECKS list, and it caught drift on its first run. It compares BYTES, not dates, over the 51 files the builder copies verbatim: the 47 control-room modules under sdk/chief_engineer, the four launcher files under scripts/laptop_bundle, and the three static pages that move into site/. It compares nothing else on purpose, and the reason is written into the check: the recorded missions, the artifacts those recordings point at, and the credentials and lab-stats snapshot are DERIVED at build time, and the snapshot is derived deliberately because copying its small inputs re-grades three bodies upward and makes the bundle claim more than the box does. A derived file would report drift on every build and the check would be ignored inside a week. A file absent from the bundle FAILs on its own, per the gate: a stale module still answers and an absent one takes a page down with an import error. A file shipped that no longer exists in the tree is a WARN and is named. First run, 2026-08-01: 0 missing, 51 compared, 4 behind the tree, named individually as sdk/chief_engineer/agenda.py, credibility.py, lab_stats.py and server.py. The bundle was built 2026-07-31 20:34 UTC and three of those four modules changed after it. The check reports and does not repair, which is this file standing rule; rebuilding the bundle is a separate decision and is not taken here.

proposals.objective: Write down that a packager which infers its contents will miss anything built at run time

The builder decides what to package by scanning recordings for interface paths, and the control room composes the certificate path in the browser from an event, so the scan matched nothing.
