GATE MET on its first clause: the mechanism is NAMED at subsystem level, the convicting discriminator is M1, and all three discriminators are recorded with outcomes besides. The defect is DAFoam v5's parallel reverse-mode AD transposed-Jacobian product -- the matrix-free adjoint operator itself (dRdWTMatVecMultFunction global tape, and equally calcJacTVecProduct) -- which under decomposition is not the transpose Jacobian of the discrete residual it claims to differentiate. Convicted by the cross-residual, exactly as the pre-registered prediction said: the converged scotch np=4 psi, mapped to serial ordering by exact integer addressing (map validated at 2.7e-15 on duplicated primal phi states), leaves a true residual of 329x ||b|| under the np=1 operator against the serial arm's own 1.14e-04 floor, unchanged to six printed digits when the serial operator is linearized at the scotch arm's own mapped state -- while the same psi satisfies its own scotch-evaluated operator at 1.2e-03 and its KSP finishes at 1.7e-07, PetscConvergedReason 2. Same vector, two operators, five orders apart: GMRES solves the wrong system exactly, which is why four orders of tolerance tightening never moved the answer. The error concentrates in U-momentum rows of partition-interface cells (13 of 15 entries above 0.5 sit on scotch boundary cells, largest 42.2, all cellLevel 0), is not a rank-corner effect (the worst cells touch one foreign rank through one face), and follows cut orientation exactly as the verified table's own hierarchy does (x-normal slabs 0.00054 percent, y-normal 0.47, scotch jagged 8.95; the worst offenders sit on y-normal processor faces). proposals.objective: Stand up the Taylor Green vortex at Reynolds 1600 as the lab's externally graded unsteady dissipation instrument: two coarse rungs on the proven transient incompressible stack, no turbulence model, graded on the kinetic energy dissipation history against the published spectral reference at a tolerance declared before any solve

That is exactly the instrument the pitching aerofoil family and the transient rotor branch will inherit: both report statistics of unsteady fields, and neither has a sibling anywhere in the lab where the transient integration itself has been graded against an external reference. Prediction, written before any solve: the coarse rung underpredicts the peak dissipation rate, because under resolution removes the small scales the peak lives on; the peak time lands within the declared tolerance at the fine rung; and the fine rung error is smaller than the coarse rung error on both quantities. One variable moves per rung, the mesh; the time step follows the declared Courant number, and a halved time step control at the coarse rung is priced in to separate temporal from spatial error before the mesh trend is read. proposals.objective: Separate the two candidate explanations for the periodic hill's finest rung refusing to converge, by testing the cheap numerical one before the interesting physical one: retighten under-relaxation on the same mesh first, and only if that fails, run the same mesh unsteady and look for a Strouhal number in the residual plateau
proposals.rationale: The 2026-08-05 in-house periodic hill ladder produced an anomaly nobody had registered a prediction for. Three rungs at 7,728, 15,600 and 31,280 cells agree on a reattachment length of 7.6436, 7.6472 and 7.6546 hill heights, a spread of 1.4 percent over a fourfold cell range, and two of the three print the solver's own convergence sentence. The fourth rung at 62,400 cells, built by the same generator, passing the same mesh gates at max non-orthogonality 39.80 and max skewness 0.118, does not converge and its residuals do not fall: sampled every 500 iterations the initial residual on Ux sits at 1.17e-2, 1.27e-2, 1.73e-2, 1.07e-2, 7.3e-3, 6.5e-3, 8.1e-3, 1.06e-2 and on pressure at 0.214 through 0.297, a limit cycle four thousand iterations wide and three to four decades above where the coarser rungs stood at the same count. Two readings fit and the results record refuses to choose between them without evidence. The physically interesting one is that at this resolution the separated shear layer stops admitting a steady solution, which would make sense of a case whose reference data are time-averaged LES of a genuinely unsteady flow, and would mean every steady RANS periodic hill result in the literature exists only because its discretization was diffusive enough to suppress the unsteadiness. The dull one is that the relaxation factors of 0.5 on velocity and pressure and 0.7 on the turbulence quantities are the benchmark case's own, tuned at the shipped resolution, and a mesh four times finer simply needs tighter ones. Prediction, written before the run: the dull explanation will NOT account for it, because a relaxation-limited SIMPLE solve usually diverges or crawls rather than sitting on a flat plateau for four thousand iterations, but it is one cheap run and the order matters, because declaring an unsteadiness finding that a relaxation factor would have removed is the kind of claim this lab has had to retract before.
citations: The F6b ERCOFTAC results record of 2026-08-05, section 4, which states both readings and refuses to choose
The F6b ERCOFTAC pre-registration of 2026-08-05, whose gates this anomaly does not disturb

Frohlich, Mellen, Rodi, Temmerman and Leschziner, Highly resolved large-eddy simulation of separated flow in a channel with streamwise periodic constrictions, Journal of Fluid Mechanics 526, 19 to 66, 2005
proposals.cost_basis: measured for run one and estimated for run two. Run one is the identical mesh and iteration cap as the rung that produced the anomaly, whose cost is recorded in this campaign's own results file, so it prices at that rung's measured core-minutes. Run two is an unsteady solve on the same 62,400 cells and is estimated, not measured; the lab's one relevant measurement is that a pitching-airfoil case on a mesh smaller than its steady sibling ran 15 to 25 times longer in wall time at a Courant-limited time step, so an unsteady periodic hill could overrun this figure substantially and the item should report a partial result rather than spend past it
proposals.expected_knowledge_gain: Either answer changes what the lab may claim about steady RANS on separated flows. If it is numerical, the ladder gains a fourth rung and the reattachment number is confirmed grid-insensitive over an eightfold cell range instead of a fourfold one. If it is unsteadiness, the finding is that the steady periodic hill solution is an artifact of insufficient resolution, which bears directly on the closure challenge because the periodic hill is its training-case class and every correction fitted to a steady baseline inherits the assumption that a steady baseline exists
proposals.launch_prompt: F6b periodic hill, the finest rung will not converge. Read demo-output/website/campaign/F6b_ERCOFTAC_RESULTS.md section 4 first, then the pre-registration. DO RUN ONE FIRST AND DO NOT SKIP IT even though the interesting answer is run two. Run one: copy demo-output/website/campaign/F6b_runs/veryfine, drop relaxationFactors to p 0.3, U 0.3, k 0.5, omega 0.5, keep endTime 6000 and residualControl 1e-6, solve serially with setsid and poll the log inline. If it converges, the anomaly is numerical: add the rung to the ladder in F6b_runs/gate.py, report the four-rung grid sensitivity, and make NO unsteadiness claim. Only if run one fails: run two, pimpleFoam on the same mesh with a Courant-limited timestep, long enough for ten shear-layer periods, with a probe in the shear layer and the bottom-wall force written every step; report the dominant frequency and its Strouhal number on hill height and bulk velocity, or report that there is no dominant frequency, which is a third answer and must not be forced into either box. Budget 55 core-min total, 2 cores, and report a partial result rather than spending past it -- run two is an estimate and unsteady cases have overrun this lab by 15 to 25 times before. Pre-register the prediction for each run before launching it. Record: evidence file in demo-output/website/campaign/, docket update on this item, honest verdict.

proposals.objective: Explain the single component -- idx16 of shapexUpper -- that the corrected warp moves further from the finite difference on the U-bend, now that 26 of the other 27 are clean
proposals.rationale: The airfoil's shape-derivative defect was resolved today and traced to the mesh warp's own linearisation. The U-bend was then tested against the same mechanism and CLEARED: its design variables are all single-point, and its two sign-flipped components agree with a finite difference of the warp to 0.32 to 1.30 percent. Yet its real verification still fails badly, at 46.6 percent aggregate with only 5 of 27 components in band, and it carries the same immunities that misled the airfoil investigation for months: a step-size sweep excludes truncation error, and tightening the primal made it worse rather than better, taking two sign flips to three. So this is a second, independent defect and nothing is known about it. The link-by-link isolation strategy is what finally worked on the airfoil after six wrong mechanisms, and it should be applied here rather than guessing again. Three features distinguish this case and are the natural first suspects: an internal duct flow rather than external aerodynamics, an objective that is a pressure difference between two patches rather than an integrated force, and a half model with a symmetry plane. A two-patch difference objective and a symmetry plane are both constructions that can carry a sign error. || PREMISE CORRECTED AND ITEM RE-SCOPED, 2026-08-02, at ZERO additional compute. Every number in the rationale above is a STOCK-TOOLCHAIN number and the item was filed believing the U-bend had been cleared of the mesh-warp defect. It had not been. The clearing test compared warpDeriv against a finite difference OF THE WARP, which is precisely the quantity the degenerate branch leaves unchanged, so it could not have detected the defect it was run to exclude -- the same blind spot as upstream's sum(dXs) regression (ROOTCAUSE section 4.2b). WHAT THE PATCHED FULL TABLE ACTUALLY SHOWS (certonomous-runs/W5-regrade/a5pl_patched_checktotals.log, 2026-08-01 13:28Z, extracted 2026-08-02 by sdk/scripts/extract_a5_fd_table.py, tabulated in W5_GRADIENT_REGRADE.md section 7.2): the aggregate is 2.2372%, not 46.6%, and 26 of 27 components are inside the calibrated +/-12% band, not 5 of 27. The stock re-run reproduces the published 27-row table to every printed digit, so this is a real comparison and not a different experiment. SO THERE IS NO SECOND DEFECT SPANNING 22 COMPONENTS. There is ONE component, and it is not one of the three features this item nominated as suspects. idx16 reads analytic -3.77483865 stock and -5.04787848 patched against a fixed FD of -4.30296296: 12.2735% -> 17.3117%. It is the only entry in the whole A1/A5 record that the correction moves the WRONG way, and it is the entire residual behind the 2.24% aggregate that W5_GRADIENT_REGRADE.md section 4 recorded as 'not explained here'. RE-SCOPED OBJECTIVE: explain idx16, not the chain. The link-by-link isolation of the whole derivative chain that this item proposes is no longer the right instrument -- 26 of 27 components are clean, so the chain is fine. The internal-duct / two-patch-difference-objective / symmetry-plane suspects are all whole-case properties and none of them can single out one component of shapexUpper while leaving the other 26 at 0.02%-2.7%. RE-PRICED: the 60 core-minutes here were 'from the U-bend's own measured 26 core-minutes per full verification cycle', i.e. priced for full-chain isolation. A single-component study needs single-component probes (the -task probe path used for A5's step-size diagnostic), not full check_totals sweeps. Whoever takes it should price one probe first. STILL OPEN AND NOT WEAKENED: the STOCK verdict. Shipped DAFoam/IDWarp 2.6.2 contains no patch, 46.64% stands as published, and NOT_PASSING_REGISTER.md is untouched by any of this.

proposals.objective: Establish whether the mesh-warp linearisation defect can be avoided in practice by expressing an opposing-direction combination design variable as a weighted set of single-point variables, and whether the resulting gradient then verifies
proposals.rationale: The defect is now understood in two parts, both measured: the warp's linearisation is wrong for opposing-direction combination modes wherever they occur, and whether that reaches a real gradient depends on whether the error overlaps the objective's own sensitivity field. Single-point variables never show it -- confirmed across three cases. That suggests a workaround available today, without waiting on an upstream fix: a combination mode is a linear combination of point motions, so the same shape freedom can be expressed as several single-point variables and combined afterwards, where the chain rule is ours rather than the library's. If the reconstructed gradient then agrees with a finite difference, every blocked optimisation using combination modes becomes runnable now. Falsified if the reconstruction disagrees too, which would locate the defect deeper than the mode construction and be worth knowing for the same reason.

proposals.objective: Run the untrained QCR2000 term forward on the benchmark's duct validation case and then, under a rule frozen beforehand, on the three scored test ducts, because the whole deficit to rank 1 lives in two of them and the term that closes it needs no training at all
proposals.rationale: The deficit to rank 1 is +0.005913 on the overall and it is not spread across the board: we already beat Reissmann on four of eight cases by a combined -0.00756, while AR_1_Ret_360 and AR_3_Ret_360 alone contribute +0.01073, which is 1.8 times the entire gap. The arithmetic that follows is the whole proposal: matching the RANK-2 entry's duct scores, 0.0455 and 0.0399, and changing nothing else on the board, gives 0.056288 against Reissmann's 0.059525. Not parity, rank 1, by 0.0032, without touching the hump or the hills. Why the ducts are lost is now a measured statement rather than an inference. The board splits on one column: Reissmann and Wu-Zhang both solve a modified equation, and the three entrants at or below us all post-process a converged field. The method-priority review of 2026-08-05 reached the same finding from the literature instead of the leaderboard, reporting that inside the turbulence-closure literature its sweep found no other post-hoc velocity correction at all and that every located data-driven RANS correction re-enters the equations. Two independent lines, neither collected to say it. And on 2026-08-05 the mechanism itself was measured on this box (the W3 QCR duct falsifier record): stock SST produces duct secondary flow at 3e-16 of bulk against a reference 0.66 to 0.81 percent on all four training ducts, so a post-hoc regression is being asked to synthesise from features an entire flow structure the underlying solve does not contain. The QCR library built for the falsifier arm closes it: on the same meshes, with k and omega transport unchanged, untrained Ccr1 = 0.3 recovers 79 to 93 percent of the reference in-plane magnitude at Pearson r 0.877 to 0.953, and cuts scaled MAE by 33 to 57 percent on all four training ducts. Round 4's demonstrated failure mechanism was feature extrapolation, Re_y at 1.85x and 2.07x the trained maximum on exactly the two ducts we trail; QCR has no training range and cannot extrapolate, so the single axis that has cost this entry points does not apply to it. It also carries the smallest leakage surface of anything the lab could submit, because nothing is fitted and so nothing could have been fitted on the wrong data.
proposals.cost_basis: Measured, from this box on 2026-08-05, and the anchors are QCR arms of the same model on the same duct family: AR_10_Ret_180 at 22,090 cells and 3,000 iterations cost 8.15 core-min, AR_3_Ret_180 at 6,627 cells and 1,725 iterations cost 3.03 core-min, both recorded in the falsifier run's ledger. Scaling by cells and by each case's own shipped baseline iteration count gives AR_7_Ret_180 validation 7 plus a 7 core-min SST control, AR_1_Ret_360 1, AR_3_Ret_360 4 and AR_14_Ret_180 28, a 47 core-min subtotal, times 1.5 for the cap-stop reruns AR_5 and AR_10 already demonstrated today, times a further contingency to 95. Interpolation to the 1,000 evaluation points reuses existing round-4 machinery at zero solver cost. The library build is done and cost about 30 s of single-core compile, so unlike the two sibling W3 items this proposal has no unpriced build half: the QCR turbulence model builds first-pass clean with stock wmake against the host v2606 install and needs no DAFoam rebuild, because the stress divergence is virtual on the turbulence model and no solver is patched.
proposals.gate: The validation arm runs FIRST and is reported whatever it says: SST and QCR on AR_7_Ret_180, the benchmark's own suggested duct validation case, scored against its LES field, with the ratio recorded before any test duct is solved. Then an all-or-none application rule, frozen in writing before the test ducts run and honoured against the known round-4 duct scores, decides whether QCR ships on all three test ducts or none. The item closes when the round-5 per-case table exists from ONE scoring call with that rule honoured, or when the validation arm fails the frozen threshold and the route is recorded as declined on validation evidence, which closes it just as well and much more cheaply.
proposals.expected_knowledge_gain: Two distinguishable outcomes, both decision-changing. The central estimate transferring today's measured training-duct ratios to the published test floors is 0.0617, rank 2, with a band from 0.05905, rank 1 outright, to 0.0666, a regression on today's entry; that spread is why the validation arm is mandatory rather than ornamental. Either way the lab learns what an untrained in-PDE constitutive term is worth on the scored ducts, which is the quantity both the rank-2 parity item and the tensor-basis carrier are ultimately arguing about, and it learns it for a fraction of what either costs. The route also degrades gracefully: it contains no beta, so the S1 plateau that just re-priced the learned-beta routes leaves it untouched.

proposals.in_sample_verdict: The falsifier work this rests on is clean: four training ducts, no test duct opened, nothing fitted, no scoring call. THIS item does open test cases, and the hazard is named rather than waved through. The model itself has zero leakage surface, because Ccr1 = 0.3 is Spalart's published constant adopted untrained and no object here is fitted to anything. The live hazard is elsewhere and it is selection: we already know we score 0.0811, 0.0775 and 0.0325 on the three test ducts, so any protocol that lets those numbers choose between the QCR field and the existing ML field is test-truth-informed model selection, the same defect C2 named and refused, one level up. The all-or-none rule exists solely to remove that degree of freedom, the validation case AR_7_Ret_180 is the benchmark's own suggested duct validation case and is not a test case, and Ccr1 is never to be tuned, because the moment it is fitted the route loses the no-training-range property that is its entire advantage and acquires a leakage surface it does not currently have.

proposals.objective: Determine why one case family's adjoint fails to converge at every mesh size tested while another family converges on a larger mesh, and whether the failing family can be fixed by conditioning rather than by hardware or coarsening
proposals.rationale: This proposal was written a few hours ago around a cell-count threshold and that framing is now dead; the measurement that killed it is the reason the question is worth more, not less. Within one transonic, shock-containing, compressible case family the adjoint returns the same linear-solver breakdown at 21,840 cells, at 79,560 cells and at 99,840 cells -- a 4.6-fold range with no exceptions. Within a separate incompressible family it converges cleanly at 63,920 cells, a LARGER mesh than the smallest failing one. So the failure does not track mesh size at all, and three consequences follow. Coarsening as an escape route is definitively dead rather than merely unpromising, which retires a strategy this lab has spent real time on. Buying hardware cannot help, since the smallest failing case peaked at 5.9 GB with the host holding over 20 GB free. And the discriminator is a property of the case, with the obvious candidate being what distinguishes the two families: six transported fields including temperature, transonic, shock-containing, against four or five, incompressible, smooth. An adjoint that is ill-conditioned because the primal carries a shock would be ill-conditioned at any resolution, which is exactly the pattern observed. Testing it means attacking the conditioning directly -- scaling, equilibration, a restarted or flexible Krylov variant -- at a mesh small enough to iterate on quickly, which the 21,840-cell case now provides at seven minutes per attempt. Falsified if the breakdown survives every conditioning treatment at the small mesh, in which case the limitation is structural to this solver's discrete adjoint for shock-containing flows, and that is a finding worth publishing rather than working around.
citations: Certonomous adjoint envelope, per-family convergence measurements across a 4.6-fold mesh range, 2026-07-29
Saad, Iterative Methods for Sparse Linear Systems, on breakdown and equilibration
proposals.cost_basis: measured, from the 420-second 21,840-cell run now established as the cheapest reproduction of the failure
proposals.expected_knowledge_gain: Decides whether an entire class of cases -- transonic and shock-containing, which is most of external aerodynamics worth optimising -- is reachable by this adjoint at all. It also hands us a cheap test bed: a seven-minute case that reproduces the failure exactly, where previously the cheapest reproduction took sixteen minutes and was assumed to need a large mesh.
proposals.decision_note: Closed on evidence gathered under the Stage 1 field-inversion work and the A3 record, not by a run against this proposal.
proposals.dismiss_reason: Approved to run. The owner directed tonight that research directions be proposed, assessed and FOLLOWED continuously rather than queued, which is the authorisation this needed. It is also now the highest-leverage open question in the lab: the memory half of the envelope is settled and well fitted, and it does not matter, because the transonic family's adjoint diverges at every mesh size measured. A cheap reproducer exists at 21,840 cells and seven minutes per attempt, so conditioning experiments that were previously assumed to need a large mesh can now be iterated quickly.
proposals.outcome: Answered. The failure is a linear-solver breakdown, not a memory ceiling. The ONERA M6 adjoint returns the same breakdown at 21,840, 42,120, 79,560 and 99,840 cells, so mesh size is not the constraint and coarsening was never going to help. The NASA hump reproduces it independently: DIVERGED_NANORINF at GMRES iteration 0 with Jacobian colouring completing normally and available memory bottoming at 18.99 GB of 30. Two levers remove the NaN and neither converges, and the matrix reordering is implicated in producing it since the failing scripts use rcm where the one working tutorial uses natural. The family that does converge, field inversion, differs in that its warping component is never constructed at all.

proposals.objective: Give the model channel a measured parametric basis: propagate published k-omega SST closure-coefficient intervals through solves on the motorcycle held mesh and report the resulting drag envelope as coefficient-interval evidence alongside the current transferred estimate
proposals.rationale: The model channel today rests on closure-family spread and validation-history transfer; neither measures how much of the answer rides on the closure coefficients themselves. The Schaefer papers supply defensible epistemic intervals with named provenance for every SST coefficient (beta-star in [0.0784, 0.1024] from Wilcox's measured stress ratio, a1 in [0.31, 0.40] which may only be increased, kappa in [0.38, 0.42] from pipe-flow experiments) and show SST is the most coefficient-sensitive of the common RANS models, with beta-star dominating drag and skin friction and a1 rising wherever the flow separates - directly relevant to a bluff body carrying a rider. The recipe holds the 353,578-cell motorcycle mesh and numerics fixed, restarts each case from the converged baseline (the papers' own cost trick), and solves one-at-a-time corner cases for the five coefficients the papers found significant: beta-star, a1, sigma-w1, beta-star/beta1, beta-star/beta2, each at its interval bounds with a1 varied upward only. Ten solves at about six minutes each from measured motorcycle solve times gives roughly 60 core-minutes; the drag envelope across the set is a measured coefficient-interval band, reported as an interval (no probability density assumed), never folded into the quadrature u_val as a sigma. If the band is material against the numerical channel of plus or minus 0.00053 on Cd, a second stage promotes the top three coefficients to a 20-sample Latin Hypercube set (order-2 response surface at oversampling 2, per the papers' design) and runs the new Sobol analysis layer for variance shares, about 120 further core-minutes. Caveat carried honestly: the intervals' provenance is flow-independent but the papers' sensitivity rankings are transonic; our solves measure the incompressible separated-flow ranking locally, which is the point.
citations: Uncertainty Quantification of Turbulence Model Closure Coefficients for Transonic Wall-Bounded Flows, Schaefer, Hosder, West, Rumsey, Carlson and Kleb, AIAA Journal 55(1), 2017
Uncertainty Quantification and Sensitivity Analysis of SA Turbulence Model Coefficients in Two and Three Dimensions, Schaefer, Cary, Mani and Spalart, AIAA 2017-1710

proposals.objective: Make a reusable check that evaluates every adjoint at its own degenerate point, and run it across the stack
proposals.rationale: This defect was invisible for a specific and generalisable reason: the derivative is correct everywhere except at the one state where it is always evaluated, and the guard that breaks it exists to stop a NaN. Upstream's own test suite could not see it because the only quantity it asserts on -- the sum of dXs -- is exactly the quantity the missing term leaves unchanged, five times out of five. Both failure modes are patterns, not accidents: threshold-guarded branches in differentiated code, and aggregate assertions that a structured error sums out of. Any adjoint this lab publishes should be checked at its degenerate configuration, against a vector-valued comparison rather than a scalar one.
proposals.cost_basis: estimate; the check itself is a finite difference at an unperturbed state, which is the cheapest test in the repertoire
proposals.gate: Every differentiated code path the lab depends on is either checked at its degenerate configuration or listed as unreachable, and no check passes on a scalar aggregate alone

proposals.objective: Measure the mesh-generation noise floor and refuse a ladder whose finest increment sits under it
proposals.rationale: Two ladders built to one recipe at a constant ratio on 2026-08-02 were both defeated by a noise source no guard in this lab tests. On the NACA 0012 an independently generated mesh at the same nominal resolution -- background divisions (64 116 39) against (65 115 40), 525,692 cells against 534,106, everything else identical -- lands 1.799e-04 away in Cd, which is 408 percent of the r3->r4 increment. The fit reads that increment and returns an observed order of 24.048. On the NACA 4412 the same control lands 3.251e-03 away, 109 percent of its increment, and on the far side of it: the control reads below r3 and continues the descent the finest rung appeared to reverse, so that ladder's non-monotone verdict is not established either. Both are snappyHexMesh on a closed STL, both converged on residualControl, both at 4 ranks, so it is not iterative and not decomposition. What it is, is that the mesh generator does not produce the same mesh twice at the same nominal resolution, and above roughly 350,000 cells on these bodies the difference it makes exceeds what the next refinement step buys. This is the guard the lab does not have. uq.eca_hoekstra_band cannot know it: nothing in a cell-count and value series carries it. It has to be measured per body and stored, the way iterative_audit is stored, and then the fit has to refuse a finest increment below it -- the way it already refuses a non-monotone triple. The cheap version is one replicate mesh at the finest rung of every family, priced at one mesh and one solve each. The B-52's turn at 441,057 cells has never had one and is the first that should: it is the finding this lab published tonight and it costs about 12 core-minutes to test. R4 ran the only such control on the record, its c4b, and measured 9.7e-05 against an 8.895e-04 increment, 11 percent -- which cleared the Ahmed 25 degree and is why nobody looked again.
proposals.cost_basis: measured; one replicate mesh plus one solve at the finest rung of each of the corpus's single-knob families, priced from the two run on 2026-08-02 at 7.30 and 6.36 core-minutes at 4 ranks and the B-52's own 12.14 core-minute rung at 2 ranks
proposals.gate: Every family carries a measured mesh-generation scatter at its finest rung, and a fit refuses an increment below it with the reason named
proposals.expected_knowledge_gain: Whether the corpus's inability to close a single ladder is a property of these flows or of the mesh generator, and a guard that stops an observed order being fitted to noise. Four of the lab's five single-knob families turn or flatten at 330,000 to 525,000 cells and only one of the four has ever been checked against a replicate mesh
proposals.outcome: Measured the same night it was proposed, at 33.6 core-minutes against est_core_min 90.0, and it corrects the item's own rationale on the point that matters most. Pre-registered at demo-output/website/campaign/W3_MESH_NOISE_FLOOR_PREREGISTRATION.md, commit 438de17c, before any replicate was built; results at W3_MESH_NOISE_FLOOR_RESULTS.md; study records at b52b0a1d. NINE replicate meshes on three bodies -- four rungs each on the two wings plus one on the B-52 -- each byte-identical to its twin except the background blockMesh division triple, verified by diff -r on system/ and 0.orig/ and md5 on the STL. NACA 0012: scatter 2.599e-03 / 1.112e-03 / 4.064e-04 / 1.799e-04 at 140,545 / 224,431 / 358,430 / 525,692 cells. It FALLS monotonically and follows an inverse-square law -- scatter times N^2 reads 0.051, 0.056, 0.052, 0.050 in units of 1e9 across a 3.74x range, constant to plus or minus 6 percent, fitted exponent 2.024. The pre-registered P1 predicted the opposite and is scored FALSE. The consequence for the item's own rationale: the NACA 0012's r4 failure was NOT the noise catching up with the signal -- its r4 scatter is the smallest of the four -- it was the increment collapsing by a factor of 44 in one step, from 1.927e-03 to 4.412e-05. Mesh-construction scatter on this body is a COARSE-mesh problem refinement cures. NACA 4412: 1.015e-03 / 2.058e-05 / 2.352e-04 / 3.251e-03. No trend, no power law, a factor of 158 between best and worst, worst at the finest rung -- the opposite of the 0012 on the same generator with the same recipe. So a single scatter correction applied corpus-wide would be wrong. Two geometries, two behaviours. THE FINDING WITH THE WIDEST REACH: the coarsest rung is the dangerous one. Scatter over increment reads 1.58 / 0.68 / 0.21 / 4.08 on the 0012 and 0.87 / 0.02 / 0.15 / 1.09 on the 4412 -- at 140,545 cells an independent mesh moves the 0012's drag by 21.6 percent of its value and 158 percent of what the next refinement step buys. Every three-rung ladder stored in this corpus puts two of its three rungs at or below that resolution, and all three replicates ever run before tonight -- R4's c4b and both wing r4b's -- were at the FINEST rung, which on the 0012 is where this generator is most reproducible. B-52 rung7b at 441,079 cells, 22 cells and 0.005 percent from rung7, reads Cd 0.050134753 against 0.048220173: scatter 1.9146e-03, 47 percent of the increment the turn consists of and 53 TIMES the rung's iterative 2-sigma of 3.584e-05. The turn's SIGN reproduces -- both fall below finer2's 0.052275 -- and refitting the five-rung family on rung7b returns the same verdict field for field, monotone false, no order, reportable_band None, with only band_abs moving 0.005069 to 0.003378. So the B-52 finding published at db89139c stands, now with a mesh-construction uncertainty attached that was not there before. b52.json's iterative_audit has since 2026-07-31 been measuring the smaller of the two noise sources by two orders of magnitude. WHAT THE GUARD SHOULD BE, corrected by the measurement: per-RUNG and not per-ladder, because the 0012's r3 is clean at 21 percent while its r1 is not at 158; and the replicate to run first is at the COARSEST rung, which is the opposite of where every replicate so far has gone. The fit itself still cannot infer any of this from a cell-count and value series, so it has to be stored, and that part of the item stands unchanged. P2's stated consequence -- that failing it would mean these ladders never measured discretization at any rung -- is corrected rather than asserted: the 4412's r2 and r3 and the 0012's r3 are clean at 2, 15 and 21 percent.

proposals.objective: Rebuild Ling's tensor-basis neural network and run his own Reynolds-number-generalisation experiment on the closure challenge's duct family: train on AR_1, AR_3, AR_5 and AR_10 at Ret 180, hold AR_7_Ret_180 for hyper-parameters, and predict the three scored duct cases without opening them
proposals.rationale: Ling, Kurzawski and Templeton trained on a duct at Re_b 3500 and tested on a duct at Re_b 2000, a Reynolds-number generalisation inside one geometry family. The benchmark's duct split is that same experiment: AR_1_Ret_360 holds the aspect ratio fixed and moves the Reynolds number, and AR_14_Ret_180 does the reverse and extrapolates beyond the trained aspect-ratio range of 1 to 10. The duct is where this lab's deficit to the rank two entry is largest, and it is the one family where the full ten-tensor basis is live, since the secondary flow is three-dimensional. The Sandia reference implementation is public under BSD-3-Clause. This proposal reproduces the architecture and the experiment design; it explicitly does NOT reproduce the paper's Table I, because two of the six training flows behind those numbers are Sandia and Stanford internal simulations with no public archive named in the paper, so the training database cannot be assembled from the paper. That non-reproducibility is itself the recorded finding of the reading.
proposals.cost_basis: measured, from this lab's own hardware, plus one stated extrapolation. Ladder-B rung B2 timed the benchmark duct primals serially on this box: AR_1_Ret_360 at 8 s (0.13 core-min) and AR_3_Ret_360 at 76 s (1.27 core-min), both runs completed and agreeing with the benchmark's shipped baseline field. AR_14_Ret_180 was not timed; scaling AR_3_Ret_360 linearly by cell count (8,748 to 31,819) gives roughly 5 core-min and is labelled an extrapolation, not a measurement. Propagation on all three scored cases is therefore about 7 core-min per model. The balance is feature and label extraction over the 57,434 training and validation cells and pointwise training of an 8-layer, 30-node network on CPU. The paper reports NO compute cost of any kind, so no part of this estimate is taken from it. Ling's Spearmint Bayesian hyper-parameter search is deliberately out of scope and unbudgeted: its cost is undisclosed and this proposal uses the paper's own stated values instead, 8 hidden layers, 30 nodes, learning rate 2.5e-7.
proposals.gate: Out of sample by construction and checked, not asserted: sdk/scripts/closure_in_sample_gate.py must return PASS with the training declaration present, and the three scored duct cases AR_1_Ret_360, AR_3_Ret_360 and AR_14_Ret_180 must never be opened for training or validation. Second gate, a priori before a posteriori: the TBNN must beat the k-omega SST baseline on RMSE of the anisotropy tensor b against the held-out AR_7_Ret_180 LES field before any solver modification is attempted. Third, the DNS-b control of the paper's section IV.B must be run alongside any propagation, so that closure error is separated from k and omega transport error rather than conflated with it.
proposals.expected_knowledge_gain: The second rung of the M2 reproduction ladder, standing up on data already in the tree. It also answers a question the taxonomy in docs/research/CLOSURE_METHODS.md left open by ranking TBNN on code availability alone: whether an invariant tensor-basis network trained only on low-Reynolds ducts transfers to the scored ducts at all. A negative result is worth as much as a positive one and costs the same hour.

proposals.objective: Reproduce step one of SpaRTA on the curved backward-facing step: extract the two additive model-form corrections b_ij^Delta and R from the shipped LES fields by k-corrective-frozen-RANS, add them back as static fields to a k-omega SST solver, and hit the paper's published Table 1 row for CBFS13700
proposals.rationale: Three facts found by reading the paper in full make this the cheapest genuine rung on the M2 ladder. First, k-corrective-frozen-RANS needs no adjoint and no optimiser: it solves the omega transport equation passively with Ui, k and bij frozen at their high-fidelity values and takes the k-equation residual as R, converging in the authors' words after a few hundred iterations. Every blocker on this lab's field-inversion line, the warpDeriv defect and the gradient conditioning, is therefore irrelevant to it. Second, the benchmark ships SpaRTA's own case: the paper states the CBFS mesh is 140 by 150 cells and the clone's polyMesh header reads nCells 21000, which is that product exactly, and each case directory carries 0/U_LES, 0/k_LES and 0/tauij_LES, precisely the three full fields the method consumes, on the same mesh, with no interpolation. Third, there is a published number to hit, so this is a reproduction and not an exercise. proposals.objective: Locate the Reynolds number at which a two-dimensional cylinder wake stops producing a time-mean recirculation bubble, by running the single intermediate rung that halves the interval in which the transition is now known to lie
proposals.rationale: Measured tonight across three rungs, all extracted by identical code against a definition confirmed word-for-word in the reference literature: mean recirculation length 0.397 diameters, then 0.254, then none at all. The third is a departure from the trend, not a continuation -- extrapolating the first two predicts about 0.165, and the method resolved 0.254 cleanly one rung earlier, so it would have seen 0.165. The mechanism is measured rather than assumed: reversal FREQUENCY is flat across all three rungs at 34 to 48 percent, while the amplitude of forward-going excursions grows from 0.22 to 0.52 to 0.81, so the bubble is swamped in the average rather than extinguished in the flow. Meanwhile the three-dimensional bubble GROWS with Reynolds number over the same interval, so the two dimensionalities diverge rather than one merely lagging. The transition therefore sits inside a factor-of-two window and one intermediate rung halves it. A falsifiable prediction is already recorded: the intermediate rung either shows a detectable bubble near 0.16 to 0.20, supporting smooth extinction reaching zero close to the upper rung, or shows none, placing the onset lower. Either outcome is decisive, which is the property a rung should have before it is worth its compute.

proposals.objective: Determine whether a gradient computed on a coarse adjoint mesh is accurate enough to drive optimization on a fine primal mesh, by measuring gradient direction agreement (cosine similarity, not just magnitude) between coarse and fine adjoints on the one case where both are affordable
proposals.rationale: The adjoint memory wall blocks four cases and the reflex response is to buy a bigger machine. That may be the wrong purchase. Optimization does not need an accurate gradient magnitude; it needs an accurate gradient DIRECTION, because the line search recovers the step length. If the coarse-mesh adjoint points the same way as the fine-mesh adjoint, the wall stops being a blocker and becomes a cost-management technique, and it does so on hardware we already own. A4 already exercises this pattern informally, using a 2,777-cell adjoint mesh against a 45,760-cell primal, but nobody has measured whether the resulting direction is right - only that its magnitude lands within 10.04 percent on a single scalar design variable, which says nothing about direction in a many-variable space. The measurement wanted is cosine similarity across the full design-variable vector at several coarsening ratios, on a case small enough that the fine-mesh adjoint is affordable as ground truth.

proposals.objective: Replace the duct correction's scalar-invariant inputs with a tensor-basis carrier, because the invariants are provably three-dimensional on a duct while the basis tensors are not, and grade it on the suggested duct validation case before any test score exists
proposals.rationale: Re-derived this session on all eight duct cases: the third scalar invariant and the fourth are zero to machine precision, the second is the exact negative of the first to the last bit, and the fifth is minus half the first squared to three parts in ten thousand million million. Five of the seven inputs therefore carry one independent number on a duct, because the baseline solve is exactly unidirectional and its velocity-gradient tensor is pure shear. The current duct model predicts three Cartesian correction components from those scalars, so it has no carrier of direction at all. The tensor basis does: measured on two duct training cases, the second basis tensor has 1.87 to 2.36 times the norm of the first, and 71 percent of its magnitude and 91 percent of the third tensor's sits in the transverse block, which is the block that generates the secondary flow a linear eddy-viscosity model omits. That is the specific structural reason the duct family belongs to the tensor-basis ansatz rather than to a scalar regression, and the sparse regression machinery to build one was measured working on this hardware earlier today. The duct deficit is where the remaining gap to first place lives: matching the best published entry on the two aspect ratios we trail would move the overall score by about 0.011, which is more than the whole gap.

proposals.objective: Determine how tight the model-form uncertainty band on hump reattachment can be made while still containing the experiment, by replacing the extremal anisotropy limiting states with physically weighted perturbations and measuring the containment/width trade-off curve
proposals.rationale: The D9 result is the lab's flagship epistemic claim: the band contains the known +13.95 percent reattachment error, and the prediction that it would was written before the runs. But the band spans 0.5278 to 1.2534, a factor of 2.4, and the record says plainly that containment is necessary and not sufficient. The band's width comes from channel 3 taking the barycentric map's extremal limiting states, which are bounds by construction and are not predictions. The open question, stated in the record itself, is not whether the band contains but how tight it can be made while still containing. That is a research question with a curve as its answer, not a single number: sweep the perturbation magnitude from extremal down toward zero and find where containment breaks. The point at which it breaks is itself the interesting result, because it measures how much of the band is doing real work. Channel 2, documented model bias from the literature, was never incorporated and belongs in this study.

proposals.objective: Propagate a Gaussian random field of eddy-viscosity log discrepancy through the periodic hill and answer the only question that decides whether the band is worth anything: does the two sigma band contain the truth on a case the statistics were not fitted on
proposals.rationale: The third step of Dow's method is propagation, and it is the step where his own work returns a negative result he discloses himself. On a straight channel, with the statistics fitted at one friction Reynolds number and applied unchanged at two higher ones, he reports the reference profile mostly inside the two sigma band. On two-dimensional random geometries the same machinery fails in the unsafe direction: his own words are that the reference profiles typically fall outside the intervals and that the estimated level of uncertainty is too low, which he attributes to a flat one parameter scaling of the field magnitude against the strain rate norm. Neither artifact prints a coverage number anywhere, so there is no published fraction to inherit and any number the lab quotes has to be its own. That is the gap this item fills, and it fills it on a case where the cost is measured rather than guessed: the earlier ensemble study propagated forty members through this same case and billed 135.47 core-min at the lower dispersion, a median member of 3.23 core-min, and it left behind an ensemble builder, a field injection path and a null test that recovered the baseline reattachment to one part in ten thousand. The truth for this case is a published large eddy simulation reattachment, and the same study already placed two other bands against it, so a third band arrives with two predecessors to be compared against rather than into an empty column. One rule from that study is adopted unchanged and pre-registered here rather than rediscovered: residual gating discarded exactly the members nearest the truth, the twelve gated members averaging 5.556 in reattachment against a truth near 4.6 to 4.7 while the twenty-eight kept members averaged 6.695, so the ungated ensemble is what gets reported. The case is a benchmark training family and no scored test case is opened.

The estimate carries no allowance for oversubscription, and the earlier pre-registration measured four ranks on two cpus billing 8.0 core-min against 6.1 for the same solve, which is the way this number goes wrong
proposals.expected_knowledge_gain: Four distinguishable outcomes. A band that contains the truth at a stated coverage and is no wider than the deterministic union it replaces is the first probabilistic band this lab can defend, and it makes the uncertainty layer a product surface. A band that contains the truth only by being much wider repeats what the random matrix study already measured, and says the fitted magnitude carries no information the two point union did not. A band that misses the truth reproduces the source method's own two-dimensional failure on a different geometry with a different solver, which is a publishable confirmation that the failure is in the method rather than in his implementation. A band that misses in the safe direction, too wide and off centre, indicts the transfer of statistics between cases rather than the sampling, and sends the next item back to the fitting step

A hardened configuration completed only at first-order convection, which is not submittable. Every workshop grid this lab now intends to read arrives in the same family, so the question is whether the numerics or the grids need to change.

proposals.gate: A second committee grid either solves at second order or fails the same way, with its mesh metrics beside the first
proposals.expected_knowledge_gain: The lab just gained the ability to read these grids and has one measurement suggesting it cannot solve on them
proposals.outcome: Executed 2026-08-01 07:56-09:43Z, and the record was written and committed while this item still sat at proposed: it was never approved and never marked, which is the finding w7-nothing-closed-while-the-box-was-full was filed to chase. The second committee grid is DPW5 unstructured_grids.REV01 level L1.T, published by the committee as hex, prism and hybrid over one shared 660,177-node distribution, so element topology varies and nothing else does. checkMesh on this box gives average non-orthogonality 23.71 / 33.57 / 51.85 and severe-face fractions 0.59% / 6.70% / 29.12%, against HLPW6 3a at 42.24 and 19.30% and this lab's own A6 CRM mesh at 18.93 and 0.00006%, one severe face in 1,751,888. Under the identical numerics that diverged on HLPW6, the hex grid ran 200 of 200 iterations at exit 0 with the Ux residual falling 1.0 to 1.4e-5; prism died at iteration 143, HLPW6 at 16, hybrid at 11, all exit 136 SIGFPE in the same Foam::divide symbol with 21.6 GiB of host memory free at the crash, so none of them is a resource failure. The answer is therefore neither yes nor no. Committee grids in tet-dominant families do generally defeat this cell-centred configuration and HLPW6 was mid-range rather than an outlier, but the hex family solves at second order with no tuning, and the ordering that predicts the outcome is non-orthogonality alone: aspect ratio and skewness both rank DPW5 hex worst of the five and it is the one that solves. Twenty configurations were tried on the hybrid grid, including HLPW6's own hardened configuration copied byte for byte, and all twenty diverged inside 29 iterations, so this is a discretisation problem and not a settings problem. Cost: 1,175.0 core-minutes over 40 instrumented runs against a 120 core-minute estimate, 9.8x under, which is the largest calibration miss now on the lab's record. Evidence: demo-output/website/committee-grids/COMMITTEE_GRID_NUMERICS.md sections 2 to 5, demo-output/website/committee-grids/measurements.jsonl, and the logs under /home/ubuntu/certonomous-runs/dpw5-committee-probe/logs/.

proposals.objective: Localize the decomposition-dependent term in DAFoam's parallel adjoint properly, and find how far the defect reaches across published cases
proposals.rationale: A4's whole unattributed gradient error turned out to be its mesh decomposition. At fixed rank count 4 the analytic gradient moves from 2.2086e-01 under DAFoam's default scotch to 2.4220e-01 under simple 4x1x1, agreeing with its own finite difference to 5.4e-06, while the converged baseline CD is invariant to five significant figures and the FD column spans 0.36%. It is converged and wrong, not under-solved: gmresRelTol tightened four orders leaves it unchanged to five digits. WHAT IS ALREADY SETTLED, 2026-08-02, so this item does not redo it. A1 at np=1 against np=4 is invariant to six digits. A5 under scotch against simple 4x1x1 at fixed np=4 differs by 2.3576e-04 / 2.9973e-04 / 3.4623e-04 in norm across its three 27-component upper-surface DV groups, worst single component 0.75%, nothing above 1%. Both are conformal meshes; A4 is the only case in either ladder carrying snappyHexMesh hanging-node refinement. TWO CANDIDATE MECHANISMS ARE DEAD. Processor boundaries landing on refinement interfaces is refuted BACKWARDS: decomposePar -cellDist plus owner/neighbour/cellLevel over all 7,843 internal faces shows scotch cutting 4 refinement interfaces and simple cutting 68, so the decomposition cutting seventeen times more of them is the one that gets the gradient right. Jacobian colour count does not discriminate either (1294 on the best configuration, 1343 on the worst, 1393 on a clean one), nor does GMRES iteration count. AND ONE ATTEMPTED LOCALIZATION IS RETRACTED, which is why this item needs doing properly. A norm hook on DAFoamWarper.compute_jacvec_product appeared to show dCD/dXv already differing by 2.98% before IDWarp is called, which would put the defect in DAFoam's parallel adjoint. That inference is NOT established: the norms are sums of squares allreduced across ranks, and volume-mesh points on processor boundaries are duplicated -- 12,276 DOFs under scotch and 12,462 under simple against a true 10,983 at np=1 -- so the intermediate rows compare differently double-counted vectors. Only the scalar dCD/dshape row, 8.81%, is partition-independent. A correct localization needs deduplication through each processor's pointProcAddressing plus a determination of whether DAFoam's convention at shared points is a partial contribution to be summed or a replicated value to be picked. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND A4: every multi-rank gradient this lab has published was computed under the default scotch. A2 is now also cleared -- compute_totals under scotch against simple 4x1x1 at fixed np=4 gives converged primals agreeing to 2.3e-05 (CD) and 5.3e-07 (CL) and gradient norms agreeing to 2.6503e-04 (CD/shape, 96 components) and 2.0065e-04 (CL/shape), with the only two components above 1 percent carrying 7.1e-04 of the gradient norm between them. That also means the W4 A2 reproduction and regrade are not themselves decomposition artifacts, which was a real risk since both they and the published run were np=4 scotch. The two sail cases and naca4412 remain unchecked.
proposals.cost_basis: measured, and revised down because A1 and A5 are already cleared: an A4 check_totals arm costs 2-6 core-min, A5's adjoint-only pair cost 6, A1's rank pair 5; the remaining published multi-rank cases plus one conformal-versus-refined pair on the same geometry
proposals.gate: Each case tested is either decomposition-invariant or is not, with its own analytic and FD columns cited at both decompositions; and the hanging-node hypothesis is either supported by a conformal-versus-refined pair on the same geometry or reported as untested
proposals.expected_knowledge_gain: Either the defect is confined to hanging-node meshes and every other published gradient is safe, or it is not and the lab finds out which of its multi-rank results were computed on a decomposition that changes the answer

proposals.objective: Rebuild the bump family on the reference grids NASA publishes and solves on
proposals.rationale: Our bump mesh carries a near-wall spacing along the whole symmetry plane where the reference relaxes it four hundredfold, and spans it with half the cell count, giving a maximum aspect ratio of 2.1 million against the reference 4,844. The ladder also has no single mesh size, since our wall cell scales by 0.53 while the reference grids are exact point-drops of one another. The pressure component of drag has no observed order at all on our meshes, where the reference code resolves it at 2.91 on the same case. HARD: wall-bounded separated flow against a maintained validation reference.

proposals.gate_correction: Recorded 2026-08-02 06:25 UTC, WHILE THE FINEST RUNG WAS STILL RUNNING, so it is not a gate moved after seeing the answer. This item's gate as written -- an observed order inside the theoretical range on the pressure component -- is UNREACHABLE. CFL3D's own published values on these same three grids, put through the same uq.eca_hoekstra_band(dim=2) call this ladder is graded by, return observed order 2.913 on the pressure component and 3.095 on total Cd, both monotone and both NOT CONCLUSIVE because order_window is 0.5 to 2.5. A solve reproducing the reference exactly would fail this gate. The viscous component and Cf at x=0.75 pass at 1.619 and 1.643, so the gate is not simply too tight for everything on these grids, only for the component the item exists to recover. The ladder is therefore graded against W1_PREREGISTRATION.md, which was committed before any solve and asks the careful question: that the cdp increments be monotone and that the fit return a finite observed order, saying nothing about that order landing inside the window. The item remains worth its cost, because our blockMesh ladder has NO order on that component at all, its increments changing sign at every matched iteration count, while CFL3D's is merely outside the window; those are different failures and moving from the first to the second is a real result. Full working in demo-output/website/campaign/W1_bump_nasa_grids.md section 5.
proposals.outcome: OUTCOME 1, THE MESH WAS THE PROBLEM, on the pre-registration's own terms; the docket gate as written was unreachable and was recorded as such in gate_correction while the last rung was still running. The 353x161 rung settled at iteration 26,996, peak-to-peak 2.997e-07 over its trailing 2,000 against a 3e-07 tolerance, exit 0, against a pre-launch prediction of 26,600 -- 1.5 percent out. On grids that are exact point-drops of one another, r = 2, one rank throughout at 3,520 / 14,080 / 56,320 cells per rank: the PRESSURE component's increments are MONOTONE at -7.250e-04 then -7.886e-05, where on our blockMesh family they changed sign at every matched iteration count, and the fit returns a finite observed order of 3.200 where that family returned none at all. W1_PREREGISTRATION.md outcome 1 asked for exactly those two things and both are met. The direction test is met too: against CFL3D on the same grids our pressure component runs -19.78, -16.77 and -11.38 percent, converging monotonically rather than wandering, and the viscous drag agrees with CFL3D to 0.04 percent on the finest rung with Cf at x=0.75 within 1.70 percent. THE GRADE IS STILL NOT CONCLUSIVE and the reason belongs to the grid family rather than to us: order_window is 0.5 to 2.5, ours is 3.200, and CFL3D's OWN pressure ladder on these same three grids fits to 2.913 and is refused by the same guard, so a solve reproducing the reference exactly would also fail. Total Cd fits 4.037, likewise refused. The viscous component fails a different guard, extrapolation_sanity, landing 0.216 of its fit range beyond its finest rung where the allowance is EXTRAPOLATION_TOL_FRAC 0.15 and CFL3D lands 0.118. COST: measured 299.74 core-minutes from the solvers' own ExecutionTime, 288.98 by the driver records, against a 180 core-minute estimate -- a 66 percent overrun, reported and not netted out. Serial throughout on purpose: four ranks at 56,320 cells would be 14,080 cells per rank and still above the 5,600 inversion, but the continuation was kept serial so a decomposition change could not perturb a trajectory already inside its settle tolerance. THREE DEFECTS FOUND AND FIXED ALONG THE WAY, none of them the item's subject. A seed-independence control the document had only asserted: the coarse rung re-solved from the medium's settled field agrees with the impulsive coarse rung to 2.50e-08 in Cd, 8.3 percent of the settle tolerance, and to 1.96e-08 on the pressure component, for 1.17 core-minutes -- and it also showed the seed buys 8.7 percent of the iterations rather than the factor the budget argument assumed. A collector reading y+ from the wrong iteration, caught before it reached this rung: postProcessing directories are named for a run's START time, the glob was unsorted, and OpenFOAM's restart rename to yPlus_<time>.dat was never handled, so the medium rung had published the y+ of iteration 5,000 beside a Cd from 16,000. And a cost-accounting bug that chained through the first run rather than the previous extension, under-reporting the medium rung by 13.67 core-minutes, 43.3 percent of its true 31.55, because that rung was restarted three times and only the last extension was counted. Full working in demo-output/website/campaign/W1_bump_nasa_grids.md sections 4 to 7.

proposals.objective: Test the matrix reordering across every blocked adjoint, since it is implicated in producing the NaN
proposals.rationale: The hump adjoint dies NANORINF at GMRES iteration zero; switching the reordering from rcm to natural removes the NaN, though it still does not converge. The failing scripts use rcm and the one working tutorial uses natural. A3, CBFS and the transonic case are all blocked with related signatures and none has had the reordering varied. One shared setting behind several independent blockers is the cheapest hypothesis left.

proposals.measured_basis: Container wall time x 4 ranks for every solve, plus offline analysis at ~1 core: CBFS 1,817 s x 4 = 121.1 core-min (including 3.7 wasted on a stale-processor abort I caused by copying an already-run case dir), M6 266 s x 4 = 17.7, offline petsc4py/scipy analysis ~890 s x 1 = 14.8. Against a 120 core-min estimate: 28% over.
proposals.outcome: Gate met on every case named, and the item's own premise is two-thirds false at zero compute. CBFS DOES change signature: rcm reproduces B3's published Total iterations: 0, PetscConvergedReason -9 exactly (87.96 s against its own 111.17 s), natural gives -3 DIVERGED_ITS after 1000 iterations (237.9 s). 21,000 cells / 4 ranks = 5,250 cells per rank. But the A3/ONERA-M6 family, transonic included, CANNOT change, because it was already running natural when it failed -- DAFoam's own runtime echo 'jacMatReOrdering natural' in its original 2026-07-28 logs (A3-onera-m6-transonic/check_totals_run1-6.log, A3-onera-m6-adjoint-coarse/check_totals_run1-3.log), before R5 touched anything. Run in the other direction to settle it by measurement rather than inference, on R5's own 21,840-cell reproducer (5,460 cells per rank): natural reproduces R5's -5 DIVERGED_BREAKDOWN (CD 400 iterations/100.87 s, CL 600/169.57 s) and rcm also gives -5, just sooner (200/200, 75.61 s and 99.06 s). No -9 anywhere in the M6 family. Different mechanism; the reordering is not a lever on it. The whole five-value ordering axis was then run on CBFS, where this lab had only ever used two: rcm -9 at iteration 0 (87.96 s) and 1wd -9 at iteration 0 (90.53 s); natural -3 (237.9 s), nd -3 (353.5 s) and qmd -3 (245.43 s), all at 1000 iterations. Two of five NaN, three stagnate, none converges, identical initial residual 7.091590452305e-04 in all five. A single buggy ordering cannot produce that split. A clean 2x2 against the standard force/CD objective (which changes dF/dW and leaves dR/dW untouched) shows the reordering controls the NaN under both objectives and the objective controls nothing; force+natural stagnates with the residual bit-identical at 5.324334345172e-02 from iteration 100 to 1000, the NASA hump's exact signature. CAUSE NAMED, and reproduced outside DAFoam entirely. Dumped the preconditioner matrix and adjoint RHS with stock PETSc runtime flags (-ksp_view_pmat binary:, -ksp_view_rhs binary:, no source change): 210,592 square, 13,710,468 nonzeros, ||b|| = 7.091590452305e-04 matching the printed iteration-0 residual to all 13 digits, no zero rows, no zero columns, no zero diagonal entries, and a diagonal spread of 8.67 decades against the M6 family's 14.17 -- so R5's conditioning mechanism does not explain CBFS. On that matrix scipy's spilu(drop_tol=1e-5, fill_factor=10) fails with 'Factor is exactly singular' (the -9, in a second independent implementation), scipy's splu with partial pivoting solves it exactly at ||Ax-b||/||b|| = 2.535461e-12 (so the system is nonsingular and consistent), and unpreconditioned scipy GMRES reproduces the stagnation at 1.0 -> 9.999687e-01 over 1000 matvecs with no DAFoam, no PETSc solver and no MPI, which exonerates DAFoam's KSP/PC configuration. One mechanism -- an incomplete factorization hitting an exact zero pivot whose destructiveness depends on elimination order -- covers both signatures and explains why B3's own pcFillLevel 4 also returned -9: fill adds fill, not pivoting. DALinearEqn.C hard-codes PCType localPCType = PCILU (and already sets PCFactorSetPivotInBlocks TRUE and MAT_SHIFT_NONZERO, which are not sufficient), so the remedy is not reachable from daOptions. Caveat stated rather than buried: the dumped matrix is the assembled preconditioner dRdWTPC, not the matrix-free transpose Jacobian GMRES applies -- the singular-ILU result is direct, the GMRES results corroborative. CORRECTED EN ROUTE, on measurement: S1_FIML_FIELD_INVERSION.md states a -5/-9 run prints 'Residual tolerance satisfied, solution finished!' and lets OpenMDAO continue. Counting the strings directly, the hump's -9 log prints that 0 times and 'not satisfied, solution failed' once; so does CBFS's; while the M6 -5 log prints 'solution finished' twice. The gate-fooling is specific to -5, where the residual collapses to denormal and reads as converged. The -9 blockers were never at risk of silently returning a wrong gradient. Net: the reordering explains the NaN on exactly the two rcm cases (hump, CBFS), explains nothing on the three M6-family cases, and unblocks none of them. The last cheap explanation is eliminated and replaced by a named, independently reproduced mechanism. Full record: dafoam/PROOF.md section 25.2-25.3, ladder-b/S1_FIML_FIELD_INVERSION.md addendum 2026-08-02, DAFOAM_CASE_STATUS.md B3 Stage 3.

proposals.objective: Test whether the anisotropy-perturbation uncertainty method destroys the very quantity it is built to bound, by establishing at what perturbation magnitude the separation bubble stops being a single closing structure and whether a converged solution exists beyond that point at all
proposals.rationale: Today's sweep produced a result more interesting than the curve it was meant to produce. Only two perturbation magnitudes met their convergence gate, and the larger of the two moved the reattachment point AWAY from the experiment rather than toward it. Every magnitude that moves toward the experimental value failed to converge, with severity rising in step, and the flow fragments into multiple separation and reattachment events from a magnitude of 0.10 onward. So the scalar the band is built on stops being well defined in exactly the range where the band would have to be tightened. If non-convergence and fragmentation are the same phenomenon, then tightening is not merely circular, it is unreachable, and that is a genuine intrinsic limit of the method rather than a failure of this attempt. Separation position stayed single-valued and smooth throughout, which extends the known separation-is-easy-reattachment-is-hard asymmetry from accuracy into numerical well-posedness. Distinguishing an intrinsic limit from a mesh-and-scheme artefact is the crux, because only the second is fixable.
citations: Certonomous hump band-tightening sweep, gate-checked points, 2026-07-29
Emory, Iaccarino et al., eigenvalue perturbation and the barycentric map
NASA Turbulence Modeling Resource, wall-mounted hump experiment

proposals.objective: Derive the NACA 0012 finite-wing reference, then re-run its ladder with the boundary layer resolved
proposals.rationale: Two independent defects sit under this credential's 148 percent deviation, and both were measured on 2026-07-31. First the reference: its drag coefficient of 0.009 was hand-set in the lab's first commit and has never been touched, its tolerance of 0.30 is hand-picked prose, and its confidence reads medium. That is the same shape as the NACA 4412 reference of 0.030 which the lab already replaced with a derivation and an RSS band. Second the solve: all three ladder rungs were meshed with layer addition switched off at chord Reynolds 1.000e6, so there are no boundary-layer cells at all, the identical defect that superseded the 4412 credential. The ladder reads 27,265 cells at 0.028688, 67,356 at 0.022290 and 140,580 at 0.012053, monotone decreasing and not grid-conclusive, and the credential grades the middle rung while the study's own working value is already the finest. On the finest rung the deviation is 34 percent, not 148. The recorded root cause, a three-dimensional wing graded against two-dimensional section data, is refuted by the wing's own solved lift: at a lift coefficient of -0.000795 on a measured aspect ratio of 3.000 the induced drag is 8.7e-08, six orders of magnitude below the section drag, so there is no induced-drag penalty here to explain the gap. Deriving at near-zero lift also removes the flaw that makes the 4412 derivation self-referential, since a reference that collapses to the section term cannot be moved by the lift error it is meant to detect. An independent anchor is already indexed for the cross-check: the NASA Turbulence Modeling Resource NACA 0012 validation, CFL3D with SST on the 897x257 grid at zero incidence, drag coefficient 0.0080937, though at Reynolds 6e6 and Mach 0.15 rather than this case's Reynolds 1e6, and computed rather than measured, so the Reynolds gap travels with it. || A THIRD DEFECT, MEASURED 2026-08-02 and not in the two this item was filed on: the 34 percent deviation on the finest rung, which this rationale correctly substitutes for the 148, is ITSELF not reproducible across mesh construction. Four meshes were built to this body's production recipe at its published resolution, differing only in the background blockMesh division triple, and all four converged on residualControl: (33 60 20) at 140,545 cells gives Cd 0.012052229 -- reproducing the stored 0.012053 to 7.7e-07, so it IS the published solve -- and (34 59 21), (32 61 21), (35 58 20) at 139,621 / 127,857 / 135,601 cells give 0.009453575, 0.010630335 and 0.009605314. Against the reference 0.009 those read +33.91, +5.04, +18.11 and +6.73 percent, so ONE of four is outside the +/-30 percent band and it is the one the wall publishes. Mean 0.010435363, sample stdev 1.1979e-03, range 2.5987e-03 which is 21.6 percent of the published value; the published mesh is the maximum of the four at +1.35 sigma. It is not a refinement effect and the direction proves it: the published mesh is the FINEST of the four and gives the HIGHEST drag, while this ladder's own trend has Cd falling with refinement. WHAT THAT DOES TO THIS ITEM. It does not weaken either defect already named -- the hand-set reference and the unlayered rungs both still stand -- but it changes what 'then re-run its ladder' has to mean. Re-running a layered ladder on ONE mesh per rung will produce another number with a 21.6 percent mesh-construction spread underneath it and no way to see it. The relayer half of this item should carry a replicate mesh at each rung, or at minimum at the rung the credential is read from. Tonight's measurement prices that at about 3 core-minutes per unlayered replicate at 4 ranks; layered replicates will be meshing-bound like the rest of this job, so the honest addition is roughly one extra mesh time per rung rather than one extra solve. AND ONE THING WORTH TESTING FIRST, cheaply, before the layered job is priced at all: the same four-mesh spread at the 358,430-cell resolution, where the measured mesh scatter is 4.064e-04 against 2.599e-03 at the published rung -- a sixth the size. TWO of the item's three parts are answered. (1) The driver of the non-monotonicity is identified: it is the mesh recipe, not the flow. The stored ladder this item names is two recipes -- coarse and medium at body level (2 3)/eMesh 2/region 1, production at (3 4)/3/2 with an IDENTICAL background mesh -- see W3_LADDER_RECIPE_AUDIT.md. (2) Removing it removes the non-monotonicity: on the valid single-knob family at 137,569 / 213,918 / 340,996 / 518,748 cells, Cl reads 0.251577808 / 0.268945377 / 0.269559189 / 0.315108812, which is MONOTONE INCREASING, and uq.eca_hoekstra_band(dim=3) returns monotone true where the stored ladder returned non-monotone. (3) The ladder still does not reach the asymptotic range, and the reason is now measured rather than hypothesised. The increments are +1.7368e-02, +6.1381e-04, +4.5550e-02 -- they fall by a factor of 28 and then rise by a factor of 74 -- and the fitted order is 34.683, outside the window. The replicate-mesh scatter measured on the SAME runs is 1.5288e-02 at r1 and 5.4805e-02 at r4, which is 88 percent and 120 percent of the increments at those rungs. So the lift increments are at or below the mesh generator's own reproducibility, and no number of further rungs on this mesh family will reach an asymptotic range. Lift is WORSE resolved than drag here: the drag scatter at r4 is 109 percent of its increment, the lift scatter 120 percent, and lift's increments are the more erratic of the two. WHAT IS NOT ANSWERED, and it is why this item stays open rather than closing. Every rung of that family is addLayers false at chord Reynolds 1.0e6, which agp-f493fff26990 named on 2026-07-31 as the exact defect for which the previous 4412 ladder was superseded on 2026-07-27. So the finding above is about THIS mesh family, unlayered, and a layered family is a different experiment with a different near-wall resolution and possibly a different floor. proposals.objective: Patch getRotationMatrix3d to the singularity-free rotation form and show the gradient comes out right with rotations still ON
proposals.rationale: The mechanism is established by subtraction -- turn rotations off and the error vanishes. That is proof of location but not proof of the fix, and it costs the boundary-layer orthogonality rotations exist to preserve. The singularity-free form R = I + [v]x + [v]x^2/(1+c), with v = a x b and c = a.b, is a polynomial in v with a smooth coefficient: correct and differentiable at a = b, no threshold, no acos, and it cannot NaN except at exact reversal, which is a real singularity of the problem rather than of the parameterization. Building IDWarp with that form and re-running the six confirmed geometries converts a diagnosis into a demonstrated fix, which is what an upstream maintainer can act on and what a five-year-old open issue has never had.

proposals.objective: Determine whether the non-asymptotic verdicts on the Ahmed body and B-52 refinement ladders come from an insufficient refinement ratio or from genuinely non-monotone grid convergence, by re-running each with a constant ratio and reporting the observed order of accuracy
proposals.rationale: Two headline geometries report ladders not in the asymptotic range, and both consequently carry conservative bands rather than extrapolated ones - the B-52 at plus or minus 0.0063 on a Cd of 0.0472, which is 13 percent, and the Ahmed body held back from the validated tier specifically because its ladder was inconclusive. The existing ladders use unequal and in places small cell-count ratios, and the B-52's rungs are non-monotone: 0.0551, 0.0448, 0.0491, 0.0472, 0.0496, 0.0523 as cells rise. Standard practice requires a constant refinement ratio to compute an observed order p at all, and without p there is no Richardson extrapolation and no grid-convergence index. The current verdicts may therefore be reporting a defect in the experiment design rather than in the solutions. This is worth settling because it is the difference between two flagship bodies being VALIDATED and not.
citations: Roache, Verification and Validation in Computational Science and Engineering
ASME V&V 20 standard on grid-convergence index
Certonomous geometry-study B-52 and Ahmed body mesh-sensitivity records
proposals.cost_basis: measured, from the B-52's own 1,267-second and motorBike's 1,022-second rebuild times; three constant-ratio rungs per body on two bodies
proposals.expected_knowledge_gain: Either an observed order of accuracy and a defensible extrapolated value for the lab's two headline geometries, or hard evidence that these flows do not converge monotonically on this mesh family, which is itself a real finding about snapped-hex meshes on complex geometry and worth publishing.

proposals.outcome: Answered, and it is the second of the two explanations offered. A constant-ratio Ahmed 25 ladder was built at one snappy recipe with the background blockMesh division triple as the only knob: 79,439 / 144,240 / 254,911 / 454,691 cells, h-ratios 1.2200, 1.2090, 1.2128 (widest pair 0.90 percent apart, against the existing ladder's 7.85), every rung solved at 4 MPI ranks. Cd = 0.084801801, 0.079359699, 0.073992743, 0.074882228. The first two increments are equal to 1.4 percent, so the fit on the coarse triple returns observed order p = 0.175 (outside [0.5, 2.5]) and a Richardson value of -0.0845, a negative drag coefficient; the fourth rung then turns back up, and uq.eca_hoekstra_band returns monotone False and refuses an order, not_conclusive_reason 'the three rungs do not move one way under refinement'. So it is NOT the refinement ratio: with the ratio constant it is genuinely non-monotone. Controls: increments are 12x to 70x the measured 1.23e-5 run-to-run floor (three prior runs of the same setup at 0.0848123 / 0.0848083 / 0.0848000); drift at each stopping point is 0.5 to 1.6 percent of that rung's increment with alternating sign; y+ falls only 331.5 to 255.1 across a 5.7x cell change and never leaves the log layer; and c4b, an independent 468,509-cell mesh at the same resolution, lands at 0.074979080, within 9.7e-5 of c4 -- 11 percent of the increment the turn consists of. The pre-registered prediction (R4_PREREGISTRATION.md G4) is scored FALSE and left as written. A sixth rung at 834,351 cells ran to endTime 4000 without converging, final-window 2-sigma 5.16e-3 = 6.26 percent of its value, above the 5 percent ceiling run_uq_studies applies, so it is refused as ladder evidence -- and iterations to convergence running 158, 212, 220, 623, 1668, then never is the likely mechanism: the steady solve stops being steady, so refining further is not the way to settle this body. The B-52 was NOT re-run and the premise was corrected instead: its fitted triple already carries a constant ratio (1.0903 vs 1.0962, 0.54 percent apart), so the proposed intervention is a no-op there; what is wrong is r = 1.09 amplifying its finest increment 4.65x against 1.24x at r = 1.30, and its increments are 253x its own iterative 2-sigma so there is real signal being amplified. Unasked-for consequence: rebased on frontal area the rungs read 0.3041, 0.2846, 0.2654, 0.2686 against the measured 0.285 -- the 45,753-cell rung that results/ahmed_25.json tiers VALIDATED at +12.95 percent is the WORST agreement in the ladder, and the solution passes through the experiment near 144,000 cells rather than converging to it; flagged for the record's owner, no curriculum JSON edited. Cost: 27.0 core-minutes at 4 ranks through c4 (0.84 + 2.00 + 3.39 + 16.74 solve, 3.8 meshing) against est_core_min 400; 70.3 more for the c4b control and 267.4 for the refused c5, all at 4 ranks. Full record: demo-output/website/campaign/R4_PREREGISTRATION.md and R4_ASYMPTOTIC_RESULTS.md.
